The 16 qualifying teams will compete over three days, with six matches scheduled each day, for the world championship title and a share of the US$3 million prize pool. The tournament will culminate in the crowning of the world champion on the final day.

Forrest Pan, Head of Global Business, highlighted the importance of delivering smooth, responsive, and stable gameplay experiences for PUBG MOBILE players. He emphasised how precision, speed, and reliable performance enable players to stay focused, react swiftly, and perform at their best in high-pressure competitive environments.

“At REDMAGIC, we believe great technology gives players the confidence to put their skills to the test,” he said. “Our liquid cooling technology helps unlock the full potential of the Snapdragon processor, while long-lasting battery life keeps players in the game. REDMAGIC’s partnership with 2026 PMGC builds on its previous involvement in China’s esports scene, extending its support for competitive gaming to the international stage. title: CAF turns profit of over $30m in 2025-26
article_text:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) governing body has recorded a profit of $31.2 million for the 2025-26 financial year.

This represents a welcome return to profitability for Egypt-based CAF, which managed this through increasing its total revenue to $284 million during the last financial year.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The governing body unveiled these figures at its 2026 general assembly in Nigeria, over the weekend.

CAF has turned its position around in the last half-decade – five years ago, it had debts of over $100 million.

This past year's figures were boosted by the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) men's national teams tournament in Morocco – over $100 million in revenue arrived through the continent's flagship event.

The soccer body's cash balance position has also improved – as of June this year, that figure came to $118.8 million.

CAF is now able to provide financial support to each of its member federations of $700,000, with this figure having most recently increased in July. Overall, the governing body has the eventual aim of taking this number up to the $1 million mark.

In terms of overall prize money and solidarity funding to African club soccer sides, meanwhile, CAF is this year contributing $48 million. In 2021, that same figure was only $19 million.

Prize money for national teams has also increased significantly over the last half-decade – the winners of the 2025 AFCON, for example, received $10 million, double what the 2021 AFCON winners were allocated.

For the Women's AFCON, the 2026 winners took home $2 million, up from just $200,000 five years ago.

In terms of recent CAF activity, earlier this month, the governing body unveiled a tie-up with sports data provider FeedConstruct.

Armenia-based FeedConstruct has snapped up exclusive match data and betting streaming rights to the full range of top-tier CAF competitions.

CAF is also looking for host nations for the next three editions of AFCON, due to be held in 2028, 2031, and 2033.

That process has a deadline of December 8 for the proper submission of all related documents and government guarantees by interested parties.

CAF, in addition, has a new secretary general, with Nigeria's Samson Adamu having recently been appointed.

title: SEN expands radio rights to A-League in Australia and New Zealand
article_text:
Sports Entertainment Network (SEN), the multi-platform Australian media company, has secured a package of domestic radio rights to the A-League, the men’s top-tier soccer competition, across Australia and New Zealand.

The deal, struck with A-Leagues, the organizer of Australia’s men’s and women’s competitions, will see SEN broadcast at least 18 regular-season A-League Men fixtures, as well as finals matches, during the ongoing 2026-27 season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

SEN’s coverage began on November 20, when Western Sydney Wanderers beat Adelaide, and aired across the SEN and Sport Nation radio networks, as well as the SEN app.

The 2026-27 A-League Men season started on October 16 and features 12 teams competing across 28 match weeks through May 9, 2027. The Final Series then starts on the weekend of June 4 to 6, 2027.

Alongside live matches, the agreement will see A-Leagues content, including player interviews and analysis, integrated across SEN’s programming in Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane, as well as Sport Nation in New Zealand.

A-Leagues chief executive Steve Rosich said: “Our focus is on introducing more Australians and New Zealanders to the excitement of live A-Leagues football.

“It’s a great boost for our game to kick off this partnership with the growing SEN network to reach new audiences and create more opportunities for sports fans to experience first-hand what makes live football so special.”

Paramount holds domestic pay-TV and free-to-air rights for the men’s and women’s A-League in a deal running through 2028-29.

Under the deal, all A-League men’s and women’s games are aired on the Paramount+ streaming service, while one men’s game is broadcast live and free on its Network 10 commercial broadcaster every week.

Network 10’s own streaming platform also houses all A-League women’s fixtures.

The new deal follows SEN’s coverage of soccer’s flagship FIFA World Cup 2026 national teams’ tournament earlier this year, the network’s third consecutive World Cup after Qatar 2022 and the Women’s World Cup 2023.

Beyond soccer, SEN holds radio rights to the Australian Rules AFL competition through 2027 and American football’s NFL, covering at least one live game per regular season and the 2026 Melbourne Game, as well as Test and Big Bash cricket matches, netball, horse racing, tennis, and golf.

SEN group content director Sam Thompson said: “Following our extensive coverage of the FIFA World Cup, we’re excited to continue that momentum by showcasing the best of our domestic competition, including some fantastic rivalries and major fixtures.

“The A-League is an important part of the Australian sporting landscape, and this agreement allows us to build on our football offering, complementing programs like Gloves Off with Bozza & Adam Peacock and giving fans more opportunities to engage with the game throughout the season.”

The new deal comes as A-Leagues continues to add to its commercial partnership slate, having brought in Champion Data as the official broadcast graphics provider for the men’s and women’s competitions last month.

title: F1 sponsors focus on contract terms as average deals hit $8.1M
article_text:
F1 sponsors focus on contract terms as average deals hit $8.1M

Ampere Analysis forecasts that Formula 1 sponsorship spend will top $3 billion in 2026. The average F1 deal costs nearly four times the average NBA or NFL deal. Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire says the old advertising-value-equivalency math has been upended. He says brands should structure deals around their end goals rather than promises of exposure.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Sports & Entertainment teams put it to work with Events & Onsite Capture.

Ampere Analysis forecasts that F1 sponsorship spend will pass $3 billion in 2026, up 15% on last season and 66% since 2022. Business Insider's Lara O'Reilly reported those figures along with a harder question from the marketing chiefs writing the checks: with this many logos on the grid, what does any one of them actually buy?

The people closest to these deals keep pointing to the contract. That suggests the rights a brand negotiates could matter more than the exposure it gets.

The scale is both the problem and the pitch. F1 now has more than 400 sponsorship partners, an average of 34 per team, and the average deal costs nearly four times the average NBA or NFL deal. A buyer paying that premium shares the car, the kit and the paddock with dozens of other brands.

Business Insider cited a 2024 academic paper finding that sponsors were more likely to renew when their team performed well, and that a larger sponsor roster was linked to a higher chance that individual brands would leave. Tim Crow, a longtime sports-marketing consultant, said F1's huge global audience includes fewer passionate fans than football or NASCAR, so brands have to work harder to stand out.

The audience still explains why brands keep paying. F1 says its global fan base reached 827 million in 2025, up 12% on the prior season, and that 43% of fans are under 35 and 42% are women. Few properties offer that mix on a calendar that runs most of the year and crosses continents.

Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire told Business Insider he sees some brands overpaying for F1 rights, which makes the market messier for everyone else. His second point matters more to anyone building a measurement plan. The old advertising-value-equivalency math has been upended, he said.

Other big sports buyers are taking a closer look too. McDonald's recently said it would end a 32-year FIFA World Cup partnership, and Heineken said last year it would end its 30-year UEFA Champions League sponsorship in 2027. Neither is an F1 deal. Both show that long-running sponsorships now face the same review as any other large line item.

McGuire's advice is to structure the deal around the brand's end goals rather than promises of exposure, and Qualcomm's own renewal shows how that works. When Qualcomm renewed with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team earlier this year, McGuire pushed for a separate agreement with driver Kimi Antonelli. McGuire says F1 is delivering strong return for the company.

Ben Cronin, editor of SportBusiness Sponsorship, reported that the addition of Brazilian driver Rafael Câmara to Haas F1's driver lineup has unlocked a sponsorship deal with Bradesco, one of Brazil's largest banks. A driver's nationality and profile can open a market for the team and the sponsor at once. That makes the driver lineup a fair topic in any negotiation, not something to wait and see about.

In B2B deals the equivalent is hospitality. Misha Sher, founder of the talent-management and brand-marketing firm One of Not Many, explained the logic to Business Insider using Oracle's partnership with Red Bull. Oracle doesn't need 100 million viewers, he said. It needs 25 decision-makers to understand how it uses technology under extreme pressure.

For a B2B sponsor, the return on an average $8.1 million F1 deal could depend on who sits in the hospitality suite.

The categories growing fastest are the ones whose products can do a visible job for a team. Ampere reports that F1 sponsorship revenue from software companies has grown 65% since 2022 and 42% since 2025. Revenue from AI-native companies is up nearly 450% since last season. Sher said brands that show how their technology helps on track get the most traction, and he pointed to Oracle with Red Bull and to Google building its Pixel phones and Gemini into McLaren's work with drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

SponsorUnited, via Motorsport.com; Ampere Analysis, via Business Insider

Motorsport.com, citing SponsorUnited, puts 2025 team sponsorship at $2.54 billion, up 22% on the previous year.

Three teams have signed wellness partners this year, Alex Harrington of Motorsport.com reported. The products are aimed as much at mechanics and engineers as at drivers, and Eight Sleep designs its beds for long-haul travel and time-zone changes. Because a wellness brand sells something fans can buy for themselves, the bigger prize could sit outside the garage, in fan activations that turn a team deal into consumer sales.

The model doesn't fit every buyer. For brands outside technology and automotive-adjacent industries, Crow said the numbers can be hard to make work. Lego and LVMH are his examples of brands that got through anyway. Lego built drivable cars for the 2025 Miami Grand Prix and the 2026 British Grand Prix. LVMH makes custom Louis Vuitton trophy trunks and supplies the Moët & Chandon the winners spray on the podium. Both made objects that became part of the race weekend.

title: AlUla, Qatar Tours cancelled, PIF pulls Jayco-AlUla cycling team backing
article_text:
The fallout from the conflict in the Middle East has continued, with elite road cycling becoming the latest sport to be impacted after the 2027 AlUla Tour and Tour of Qatar events were scrapped and AlUla withdrew from its sponsorship coverage of the sport.

The AlUla Tour, formerly known as the Saudi Tour, is the most prominent cancellation. Promoted by Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO), which organizes the Tour de France, the multi-day five-stage race has been an annual staple since 2020, and in 2026 was designated UCI ProSeries class.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In recent years, prominent names such as British riders Tom Pidcock (2025) and Simon Yates (2024) have won the event, which typically takes place across late January and early February.

It is not yet confirmed whether or not the event will return in 2028, but with the Saudi government’s focus diverting away from sport in the short term, it may be unlikely.

A return for the men’s and women’s Tour of Qatar, which has not been staged since 2016, has also been cancelled, with a new aim of 2028 announced for the race’s restart.

Eight months of conflict between Iran and a US-Israel coalition, as well as increasing tensions in Saudi Arabia with the Houthi rebel group (which has recently claimed credit for multiple attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia), have left confidence in the region from a hosting perspective low, despite the large sums of money that countries in the Middle East can dedicate towards hosting fees.

The AlUla Development Company, the commercial vehicle for the AlUla region, is owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), a sovereign wealth fund, which has pared back its sports investments across 2026.

This has affected the peloton, as men’s WorldTour team Jayco-AlUla and associated women's team, Liv-AlUla-Jayco, have been left without sponsorship.

The PIF has pulled its sponsorship of the two teams, which are predominantly backed by Australian businessman Gerry Ryan, founder of caravan manufacturer Jayco, and the eponymous Jayco brand.

Publication Escape Collective claims that Ryan has already secured a crucial new commercial partner, meaning that the team’s budget for 2026 will not be cut too substantially, although a reduction on such short notice is possible.

The team has already lost Grand Tour stage winners Ben O’Connor and Mauro Schmid ahead of the 2027 campaign.

Sponsorship such as this is vital for cycling teams at all levels of the sport, the majority of which are almost entirely sponsor-funded, meaning that losing a title sponsor like AlUla could be crippling to many operations.

Cycling’s heavy reliance on sponsorship revenue, and that spending’s direct correlation with rider contract spending, has created a catch-22 situation where winning races requires top riders, access to top riders requires significant sponsorship revenue, and sponsorship revenue can only be grown by winning races.

This has effectively stratified the WorldTour peloton, with the top six-to-eight teams, backed by high-profile sponsors, billionaire investment, or sovereign wealth financing, performing at a level that the other sides, which rely on less lucrative sponsorship deals and, in many cases, face an annual struggle just to continue operations, cannot.

This dynamic was dissected earlier this year on the Sportcal Podcast, wherein GlobalData Sport lead analyst Conrad Wiacek and head of data Gordon Berry discussed the varying perspectives on cycling sponsorship, where money in cycling comes from, and how teams can improve sponsorship values by maximizing their resources.

title: Copa America close to US return for 2028 edition
article_text:
South American soccer’s CONMEBOL is reportedly close to announcing the United States as the host of the 2028 Copa America continental competition.

The quadrennial tournament, CONMEBOL’s flagship national team competition, will be hosted in the US for the second consecutive time in 2028, and the third time overall.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The reports come after the US' successful co-hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026 earlier this year alongside Canada and Mexico, while reports from South America suggest Ecuador is not ready to host the event.

Copa America hosting rights are awarded on a cyclical basis between the CONMEBOL nations and Ecuador. Recent reports state Ecuador remains unprepared to host the event again four years after pulling out the first time.

In 2024, the US stepped in after CONMEBOL agreed to a strategic tie-up with North America’s CONCACAF that saw the US replace the initial host, Ecuador, which had to pull out due to public security issues in the country.

The US also hosted in 2016 a special edition of the tournament outside of the four-year cycle, also part of an agreement between CONMEBOL and CONCACAF to celebrate the centenary of the Copa America.

In all, this means the US has hosted three of the last five editions of the Copa America, perhaps suggesting that CONMEBOL has come to be reliant on the increased financial benefits of staging the tournament in the US.

After all, US hosting means US participation, allowing CONMEBOL to command greater rights fees in the most lucrative sports market in the Americas, and beyond.

The 2024 edition was expanded from 10 to 16 teams, adding six CONCACAF sides to the mix: Canada, Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, and the US.

Subsequently, rights were snapped up in the US by media giant Fox, which generated multiple record seven-figure viewership tallies during the tournament, despite a US exit.

The 2024 Copa América final between Argentina and Colombia, won by the former, delivered 6.35 million viewers, drawing the largest audience on Spanish-language media giant TelevisaUnivision to that point since the 2014 World Cup final.

Fox’s viewership, which peaked at 7.07 million, increased 211% when compared to the 2021 edition between Brazil and Argentina (1.94 million), and was he tournament’s largest English-language audience on record.

The Copa America tournament overall averaged 1.42 million viewers across the Fox, FS1, and FS2 channels, an increase of more than 350% from 2021’s 309,000, and up 44% from 2016’s 987,000, ranking it as the most-watched edition of the tournament on English-language TV.

Dentsu, the Japanese advertising giant heavily involved in sports marketing, remains the exclusive global consulting and commercial sales agent of the Copa America through the 2028 edition, and will likely be hoping that the event returns to the US, as it would once more be able to attract high-profile US brands to sponsor the event.

The 2024 edition was sponsored by the likes of US beer brand Michelob Ultra, soft drinks giant Coca-Cola, tech firm TCL, Chinese electric car company BYD, and consumer goods conglomerate Unilever.

title: Melbourne Storm Appoints AXS as Official Ticketing Partner Ahead of 2027 NRL Season
article_text:
Melbourne Storm has entered a partnership with global ticketing provider AXS, naming the company the club’s Official Ticketing Partner ahead of the 2027 National Rugby League (NRL) season.

The agreement transitions all ticketing sales, member access, and event management for Storm home fixtures at AAMI Park onto the dedicated AXS platform and mobile application.

The deal expands AXS’s rapidly consolidating Melbourne sporting precinct footprint, which already encompasses Melbourne Park, the newly opened AXS Fan Hub, and seven major local franchises across rugby league, basketball, football, and netball.

Commenting on the partnership, Melbourne Storm CEO, Justin Rodski, said: “Providing our members and fans with a seamless ticketing experience is incredibly important to us, and we’re delighted to partner with a trusted, global leader like AXS.”

“AXS shares our commitment to innovation and delivering great experiences for fans, and this partnership will provide our supporters with a simple and seamless way to purchase and manage their tickets to Storm games.

“We look forward to working closely with the AXS team over the coming years and delivering a ticketing experience that matches the high expectations of our members and fans,” Rodski said.

AXS Australia and New Zealand CEO, Andrew Travis, highlighted the role of frictionless live-event access in building long-term supporter affinity at AAMI Park.

“The real power of live sport is that one game can spark a lifelong connection – to a team, to a community and to something bigger than yourself.”

“Our ambition at AXS is to help Storm build those connections for generations to come.

“We want more people to discover the atmosphere at AAMI Park, feel that sense of belonging and become part of the Club’s future,” Travis said.

Beyond core primary and secondary ticketing infrastructure, the partnership integrates match-day fan experience assets designed to increase per-capita yield and supporter engagement at AAMI Park.

AXS assumes naming rights as Presenting Partner of the club’s official pre-game precinct activation, Purple Paddock, while launching AXS Seat Upgrade to enable in-venue digital seat upgrades during Storm home fixtures.

title: Alaalatoa hits 100 for Wallabies as fellow veteran ends 4-year Test exile
article_text:
Veteran prop Allan Alaalatoa will become the 14th Wallabies centurion when he runs out onto Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, against Ireland on Friday night.

Ten years have passed since Alaalatoa made his debut against New Zealand in a 42-8 defeat at the ANZ Stadium in Sydney.

He will co-captain the side with Harry Wilson, who drops to the bench, for the Wallabies’ final Test of 2026.

After patiently waiting for his first cap, Sydney-born James Ramm has been brought into the team on the wing.

A one-time Olympics gymnast hopeful, Ramm makes his debut in the country where he rediscovered his love for the game during a spell at title-winning Northampton Saints.

Now with Western Force, the 28-year-old is joined in the matchday 23 by another uncapped player in reserve scrum-half, Teddy Wilson.

The former Junior Wallabies captain in line to become the 16th son of a Wallaby to pull on the gold jersey, following in the footsteps of his father David who featured in two Rugby World Cups, including the 1999 side that lifted the Webb Ellis Cup in Cardiff.

A quarter of a century ago, his father played his club rugby across the road from the Allianz Stadium at the Twickenham Stoop after signing for the world-famous Harlequins.

Elsewhere, Kurtley Beale has earned a remarkable recall to the gold jersey – named on the bench, four years since his last Test appearance. Beale is four caps behind Alaalatoa and has made more appearances for the Wallabies than the starting back-three combined.

Kalani Thomas has earned his first Test start at scrum-half alongside club teammate, Carter Gordon.

Wallabies Head Coach Les Kiss said: “Reaching 100 Test matches for your country is a remarkable achievement and it’s only fitting that Allan leads the side out as co-captain for such a monumental occasion.

“He is a talismanic figure within the group, and I know the whole squad and support staff will be doing everything they can to make this rare milestone a memorable one for him, his family and for us.

“We’ve taken some steps forward, grown our game and tested our squad depth this year as a squad and I know the team is highly motivated to put in a performance that reflects the hard work put in by everyone in our final Test.”

title: South America Rugby World Cup 2035 Bid Takes Step Forward
article_text:
As part of the formal bidding process, a multinational working group had already completed a detailed questionnaire covering every proposed venue and host nation. The subsequent online meeting allowed the South American delegation to formally present its vision to twelve Rugby World Cup representatives joining from London and Dublin, followed by a Q&A session addressing specific inquiries.

(A). The Power of Amateur Club Culture: Officials emphasized the central social, familial, emotional, and sporting role of local clubs across the region, positioning grassroots rugby as a foundational pillar of the tournament.

(B). World-Class Tourism: Supported by a promotional video, the delegation highlighted the diverse destinations awaiting visiting fans across the four nations and wider continent—from Patagonia and Iguazu Falls (bordering three countries) to the Atacama Desert and the beaches of Punta del Este and Rio de Janeiro.

(C). Proven Event-Hosting Capacity: The bid underscored South America’s track record of successfully staging massive global gatherings, citing the Olympic Games, the Youth Olympic Games, the FIFA World Cup, major international concerts, MotoGP, Formula One, and Pope Leo XIV’s recent visit to Uruguay and Argentina, which drew millions of attendees with seamless organization.

Former Puma Horacio Agulla, a three-time World Cup veteran (2007, 2011, and 2015) and active member of the bid team, noted that the presentation was warmly received.

“Since it was a Zoom call, we could have done it from an office, but we wanted the importance and symbolism of the clubs as the center of our bid to be crystal clear. It is a differentiator that we are looking to leverage”

“We are convinced that a World Cup in our region will have full stadiums, all the appeal of tourism, and—as an X-factor—the passion and love we feel for rugby, which is born in the clubs.”

The next phase of the candidacy will be an on-site technical visit by Rugby World Cup officials to inspect each proposed venue across the region. Following that tour, additional questionnaires and evaluations will take place in early 2027 to finalize assurances before the World Rugby Executive Board selects and announces the 2035 host in November 2027.

title: Greg Fisilau to make England debut start in blockbuster All Blacks rematch
article_text:
Greg Fisilau will make his first England start against the All Blacks on Saturday with Steve Borthwick making five changes to his side for this weekend’s rematch with New Zealand, recalling Freddie Steward at full-back.

Fisilau, 23, has impressed in England’s three victories to date as a replacement and earns his first start in the No 7 jersey with Ben Curry dropping to the bench. Elsewhere, there are starts for Tommy Freeman on the wing as well Ellis Genge and Luke Cowan-Dickie in the front row.

Borthwick’s decision to start Fisilau means Henry Pollock remains on the replacements bench but it is a richly deserved start for the Exeter back-rower. He was singled out by the head coach for his cameo against Japan and has the opportunity on Saturday to further advance his claim for a place in next year’s World Cup squad.

Steward comes back into the side at full-back with George Furbank dropping out of the 23-man squad. The Leicester No 15 replaced Furbank against Japan because the Harlequins full-back was struggling with a groin problem but Borthwick has given Steward the nod for tactical reasons this weekend.

Up front, Borthwick has opted to start Genge and Cowan-Dickie with Fin Baxter and Jamie George dropping to the bench. Freeman’s recall, meanwhile, was expected after he was a late withdrawal from the 37-12 victory over the All Blacks last weekend with a thigh injury.

The rest of the squad is unchanged with Joe Heyes continuing at tighthead prop and the captain Maro Itoje partnering Alex Coles in the second row. Ollie Chessum continues at blindside flanker while Ben Earl is again at No 8 after his man-of-the-match performance last weekend.

Jack van Poortvliet stays at scrum-half with Fin Smith wearing the No 10 jersey while Seb Atkinson and Henry Slade stay at centre. Will Joseph makes his third consecutive start on the wing. On the bench, Will Stuart joins Baxter and George as front-row cover while George Martin is one of six forwards among the replacements. Archie McParland and Marcus Smith are the backs.

Borthwick’s side are chasing a record third straight victory over the All Blacks as they bid to finish third in the inaugural Nations Championship. “To have the opportunity to play New Zealand again is something the players are really looking forward to,” said Borthwick. “We know the quality New Zealand have and the challenge they’ll bring across the field. For us, it’s about building on last Saturday’s performance, maintaining the standards we set and finding that same level again.”

Meanwhile, South Africa have refused to send a coach to the Nations Championship finals weekend media day at Twickenham with only the captain Siya Kolisi expected to attend. With Rassie Erasmus serving a six-match suspension for his remarkable rant, in which he questioned whether officials were “match-fixing” this month, the Boks are the only one of the 12 competing nations not represented by a coach at the midweek event.

All nations taking part were obliged to send their coach and captain for a series of media appearances. It is understood that the Springboks will not be fined for their coaches boycotting the event before their contest the final against France on Sunday.

This week, the South Africa assistant coach Mzwandile Stick conducted a press conference in his mother tongue of Xhosa to avoid being misinterpreted. When speaking the week before, Stick made comments about the decision by a disciplinary panel to clear Sam Prendergast to play for Ireland against South Africa which could yet land him in hot water.

The fly-half was cited for a hip-drop tackle against Fiji but later cleared. Stick said: “If that was a Fijian player, he would be sitting in Fiji now doing some extra lessons of how to tackle. But it’s an Irish player, it’s free to play.”

Erasmus’s ban came after he claimed officials had missed 17 knee-drop tackles committed against his side in their defeat by France, suggesting that incidents of foul play are not being picked up in what he described as a “manipulation of the game” and that officials are showing more leniency to northern hemisphere teams.

When serving the first match of his ban Erasmus set up an 18+ watchalong in which supporters were able to view the head coach sitting in a Dublin hotel room while he watched their narrow defeat by Ireland. Erasmus has already named South Africa’s side to face France but will be forced into a change with Pieter-Steph du Toit ruled out through injury.

title: Four banned by new World Rugby ruling as Springboks boss Erasmus joined by others
article_text:
World Rugby's clampdown on the abuse of match officials has resulted in another ban.

Romania defence coach Benjamin Lapeyre has been hit with a two-match ban for "disrespecting the authority of match officials" during their Nations Cup defeat to Canada on the weekend. Romania were beaten 27-26 in Bucharest, with Lapeyre having been serving as water carrier during the match.

The former full-back - who turned out for the likes of Toulon and Brive in his playing days - was reported to have been repeatedly challenging the referee's decisions during the match, including making comments about the performance of the TMO.

Challenges were also reportedly aimed towards the assistant referee.

As part of World Rugby's new match official abuse sanction process, an independent panel will now consider such conduct and is able to issue an automatic sanction.

Having reviewed the evidence, Lapeyre's actions were deemed to amount to disrespecting the authority of a match official.

As such, he is banned from all match-day activity, including being present in the stadium, for the duration of the two-match ban.

Lapeyre is the fourth individual to be sanctioned by World Rugby's new process, which was only introduced in the summer.

The most high-profile has been Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus, who was banned for six matches with immediate effect last week.

The South African had made explosive comments in a press conference about refereeing at the start of last week, following his side's narrow defeat to France.

The match official abuse sanction process decided that Erasmus had made comments that suggested "match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match, and when the conduct is considered as a whole a reasonable person would conclude that the conduct constituted an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials".

On the same day that Erasmus was banned, Hong Kong coach Kane Hames was also hit with a six-match ban for verbal abuse during their Nations Cup match against USA.

Like Lapeyre, Hames was serving as water carrier that day - with offensive language aimed at the officials being picked up on the live broadcast.

Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada had been the first person banned under World Rugby's new guidelines back in July.

He was automatically sanctioned with a two-match ban after criticising referees in a broadcast interview following their defeat to New Zealand in Wellington.

title: Ireland's Stockdale returns as Beale, 37, back for Wallabies
article_text:
Ulster wing Jacob Stockdale has been recalled to the Ireland line-up for Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off match against Australia.

Stockdale, who was not involved in Ireland's home wins over Argentina, Fiji and South Africa, replaces Mack Hansen on the left wing.

Nick Timoney comes in for Dan Sheehan at number eight in the only other change to the line-up that started Saturday's 20-17 victory over world champions South Africa at Aviva Stadium.

Sheehan is ruled out of Friday's match at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium (20:10 GMT) after being banned for two games for a croc-roll tackle during the victory over the Springboks.

Tadhg Beirne will captain Ireland in Sheehan's absence for the second time this autumn, having also stepped up against Fiji when Sheehan was ruled out through concussion.

Stockdale returns to the line-up for his 44th cap after a strong start to the season with Ulster, with three tries in as many games.

The 30-year-old started Ireland's Six Nations defeat by France in Paris in February, and while he was not picked against Italy or England, he made a try-scoring return against Wales.

Friday will be Stockdale's first appearance in green since July's Nations Championship victory over Japan.

He is one of eight Ulster players in head coach Andy Farrell's matchday squad. Robert Baloucoune, who starred with two tries against the Springboks, is retained at right wing with Stuart McCloskey kept at inside centre.

With Sheehan out, Timoney returns to number eight. Farrell is dealing with an injury crisis in the back-row position with Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen ruled out.

Timoney started at the base of the scrum against Fiji having been preferred to Josh van der Flier at open-side flanker for the Argentina game.

Hooker Tom Stewart and prop Tom O'Toole are retained on the bench alongside Leinster's Thomas Clarkson, who have been dubbed the 'Tom Squad'.

James McNabney is back among the replacements after his eye-catching debut against Fiji was cut short by a concussion.

Nathan Doak, who like Stockdale has not been involved so far this month, is named as the back-up scrum-half.

Despite a taxing win over South Africa, Farrell has opted against making wholesale changes with Andrew Porter, Ronan Kelleher and Tadhg Furlong retained in the front row.

Joe McCarthy and Beirne are kept in the second row with Ryan Baird and Van der Flier alongside Timoney in the back row.

Despite a morale-boosting win over South Africa to round out the Nations Championship campaign with five wins from six games, Ireland finished third in the northern hemisphere standings behind France and England.

Australia finished third in the southern hemisphere table behind South Africa and New Zealand despite losing four of their six games, including a 33-31 defeat by Ireland in the opening round in Sydney.

Since that game, Joe Schmidt has been replaced as Wallabies boss by former Ireland defence coach and Ulster director of rugby Les Kiss.

Kiss has named two uncapped players in his matchday squad with James Ramm selected on the left wing and Teddy Wilson - son of former World Cup winner David - named as the replacement scrum-half.

The Wallabies bench also features 37-year-old utility back Kurtley Beale, who is set to earn his first cap in five years.

Allan Alaalatoa will co-captain the Wallabies on his 100th cap alongside Harry Wilson, who is named on the bench, while scrum-half Kalani Thomas earns his first Test start after coming off the bench in last weekend's win over Wales in Cardiff.

Ireland: Keenan; Baloucoune, Henshaw, McCloskey, Stockdale; Prendergast, Gibson-Park; Porter, Kelleher, Furlong, McCarthy, Beirne (capt), Baird, Van der Flier, Timoney.

Replacements: Stewart, O'Toole, Clarkson, Ryan, McNabney, Doak, Frawley, Aki.

Australia: Wright; Jorgensen, Suaalii, Ikitau, Ramm; Gordon, Thomas; Kailea, Paenga-Amosa, Alaalatoa (co-capt), Canham, Williams, Hooper, Tizzano, Valetini.

Replacements: Nasser, Bell, Tupou, Shaw, Wilson (co-capt), McReight, Wilson, Beale.

title: World Rugby clampdown on match official abuse leads to another ban
article_text:
Romania defence, skills and backs coach Benjamin Lapeyre has been banned for two matches for disrespecting match officials during the Oaks’ 27-26 defeat to Canada in the World Rugby Nations Cup last weekend.

Lapeyre, who was acting as a water carrier at the time, was reported as repeatedly challenging match official decisions during the match, including comments concerning the performance of the TMO and challenges directed at or towards the assistant referee.

An independent panel met and considered the comments and conduct cumulatively and determined that they collectively amounted to disrespecting the authority of a match official.

In line with the provisions of the Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, Lapeyre is banned from all match-day activity, including being present in the stadium, for the duration of the two-match suspension.

Lapeyre is the latest coach to be sanctioned as World Rugby strives to protect the integrity of match officials.

Hong Kong China scrum coach Kane Hames was slapped with a six-match ban for verbally abusing officials during their match with the United States earlier this month, while South Africa boss Rassie Erasmus was sanctioned for the same length of time following controversial comments about match officials after South Africa’s 21-19 defeat to France.

title: World Rugby confirms another ban for disrespecting match officials
article_text:
World Rugby has handed out another two-match suspension as the governing body continues its crackdown on the abuse of match officials.

Romania water carrier Benjamin Lapeyre has been banned following his conduct during the World Rugby Nations Cup clash against Canada in Bucharest on 20 November.

Lapeyre was reported for repeatedly challenging decisions during the match, including comments about the performance of the TMO and challenges directed towards an assistant referee.

An independent panel concluded that his conduct amounted to disrespecting the authority of match officials.

The decision comes amid growing concerns over the treatment of referees, with Hollie Davidson recently receiving widespread support from rugby fans following reports of online abuse.

The suspension means Lapeyre will be banned from all matchday activities for two matches.

He will not even be permitted to enter the stadium during those fixtures.

The punishment falls under World Rugby's Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, which was introduced in July 2026.

The new process allows independent panels to punish members of team personnel for inappropriate comments or conduct towards match officials.

Punishments range from guidance letters and formal warnings to suspensions.

World Rugby has previously highlighted how inaccurate comments about refereeing performances from those in positions of authority can fuel online abuse.

The latest suspension serves as another reminder that World Rugby's crackdown extends beyond players and head coaches to all members of the matchday team.

title: Springboks rocked by Pieter-Steph du Toit withdrawal as Rassie delays replacement call
article_text:
Pieter-Steph du Toit has been ruled out of the Springboks’ Nations Championship final against France, Rassie Erasmus has confirmed.

The blindside flanker has withdrawn from the matchday 23 to face Les Bleus, with Erasmus yet to confirm the changes to the team for the meeting at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham.

Du Toit will return to South Africa along with full-back Damian Willemse, who was omitted from the squad due to an injury he sustained last week against Ireland.

Earlier this week, Ruan Nortje and Ntuthuko Mchunu returned to South Africa, while veteran hooker Bongi Mbonambi linked up with the squad.

Du Toit was named in the run-on team to face France, with his injury now leaving the Springboks with a selection conundrum. Marco van Staden featured against Ireland last week and could come into the 23 but South Africa are still awaiting the verdict of his disciplinary hearing after his red card for a shoulder charge.

“Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus announced on Wednesday morning that flanker Pieter-Steph du Toit has been forced to withdraw from Sunday’s Nations Championship final against France in London due to a niggle and will return to South Africa along with fullback Damian Willemse,” a SA Rugby statement read.

“Erasmus will announce the changes to the match-23 to face Les Bleus later in the week once he has decided whether to call up a replacement player to London.”

Du Toit’s void could be filled by Emmanuel Tshituka, who was named on the bench for the Nations Championship final where he could make his Test debut. The Congo-born loose forward received glowing praise from assistant coach Mzwandile Stick earlier this week.

“We look at Emmanuel and the profile of Pieter-Steph, [who] works hard all day. He’s a world-class player,” Stick said, via Xhosa translator Kuhle “Kooks” Sonkosi.

“Manu’s the same. He’s got the same profile, and especially at the Sharks, the way he plays, the hard work he does and obviously all the work in the dark.

He added: “You look against France as well, they’re obviously going to bring physicality. Manu brings that as well.

“So that’s what Manu hopefully will do this week, and that’s why he’s been given a chance.”

title: Springboks hit by injury blow as Pieter-Steph du Toit ruled out of Nations Championship final
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

South Africa have been dealt a significant injury blow with flanker Pieter-Steph du Toit ruled out of Sunday’s Nations Championship final against France.

The Springboks blindside had been set to start the game at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium, but drops out due to a niggle.

A replacement will be confirmed later in the week with South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus considering whether to call up a replacement.

Debutant Emmanuel Tshituka has been named on the bench and was compared to Du Toit by assistant coach Mzwandile Stick on Monday.

Lock Franco Mostert has also played on the side of the scrum at times, while Erasmus, who is serving a six-match ban for comments about match officials, may also look to reshuffle his back row entirely.

Both De Toit and injured full-back Damian Willemse will return to South Africa ahead of the weekend.

Willemse has been replaced in his role by Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, with Manie Libbok brought in to the side at fly half.

South Africa are seeking to snap a two-match losing run having been beaten by France in Paris two Fridays ago.

title: World Rugby's England haka fine decision finally revealed
article_text:
England look set to escape punishment for their response to the All Blacks' haka, with common sense seemingly prevailing at World Rugby. Despite the regulations surrounding the traditional Māori challenge and the precedent set at the 2019 Rugby World Cup, no fine has been publicly announced.

Four days have now passed since England's response at Allianz Stadium, which saw players cross the halfway line.

England were famously fined £2,000 at the 2019 Rugby World Cup in Japan after adopting a V-shaped formation in response to the haka.

That decision sparked widespread criticism, with many supporters arguing that teams should be allowed to respectfully respond to the challenge.

The haka is one of rugby's greatest traditions, but the opposition's response can add to the spectacle.

Saturday's scenes generated exactly the sort of excitement and anticipation that international rugby thrives on.

With England and New Zealand preparing to lock horns again this weekend, there appears little appetite for another disciplinary controversy.

World Rugby has yet to publicly confirm its position, but common sense looks set to prevail this time around.

title: Argentina name two SVNS debutants in star-studded squad
article_text:
Two potential HSBC SVNS Series debutants have been included in Argentina’s squad for Dubai and Cape Town, with Santiago Alvarez and Luciano Gonzalez the most experienced members of a squad that has played 389 events between them.

La Plata-product Luca Julian is set to wear a Los Pumas Sevens jersey for the first time, while Francisco Calello is also set for a maiden appearance on the SVNS Series. Calello did get to play for the national sevens team at the recent South American Championship in Cordoba.

Alvarez is the most-experienced player in the Los Pumas Sevens squad, with the forward set to earn his 79th tournament cap. Gonzalez has featured in 72 SVNS events, while Santiago Mare and Marcos Moneta have played at least 42 tournaments each.

Moneta was the top try-scorer on the SVNS Series last season, while Gonzalez earned Dream Team honours after another exceptional season. Argentina didn’t win any titles last season but did claim silver twice, and bronze another two times.

Argentina have been drawn in Pool A along with two-time reigning SVNS World Championship winners South Africa, Australia, and the United States. Los Pumas Sevens get their new campaign underway against the Blitzboks at 4:52 am on Saturday morning (Argentine time).

title: Beauden Barrett nears Bristol move as a two-year deal could make him the Gallagher PREM's top earner
article_text:
Beauden Barrett is in advanced talks to sign for Bristol Bears, according to reports on 24 November 2026.

The All Blacks fly-half and full-back just hit 150 test matches for New Zealand in their heavy defeat to England in the Rugby Nations Championship at Allianz Twickenham last weekend.

Read more: When will Beauden Barrett break the All Blacks test cap record?

A deal for Barrett to join Bristol is close to completion, according to the person posting, who says they were told this.

Bristol’s formal offer is with Barrett’s management, and the club are waiting for confirmation, according to Daily Mail. The deal is rumoured to be worth more than £1 million per season for two years, and it could also make him the highest-paid player in the Gallagher PREM.

All Black sabbaticals after a World Cup or early in a World Cup cycle are common with many opting for Japan, the Top 14 in France or Leinster.

The 2015 World Cup winner only has to look to his brother Jordie for the benefits of a sabbatical with the centre having played the 2024-25 season at Leinster, where he was then able to catapult towards some of his best rugby afterwards.

Newcastle Red Bulls have already turned down the chance to sign Barrett, the New Zealander, according to Ruck. Bristol reportedly face competition for Barrett from an unnamed French Top 14 club, according to Ruck.

title: Cowan-Dickie insists England will not let up after record triumph over All Blacks
article_text:
Luke Cowan-Dickie is adamant England will not let complacency creep in after their record win over the All Blacks, insisting they will not repeat the mistakes of the 2019 World Cup.

Cowan-Dickie is one of three players, with Jamie George and Maro Itoje, who would claim a fourth career win for England against New Zealand on Saturday if Steve Borthwick’s side back up last weekend’s 37-12 victory at Twickenham. The Sale hooker was part of the squad who defeated the All Blacks in the 2019 World Cup semi-final in emphatic fashion and went into the final against South Africa as favourites. Eddie Jones’s side were comfortably outplayed by the Springboks, however, with Cowan-Dickie acknowledging that England failed to hit their emotional peak that day.

Last weekend England flew out of the blocks, inspired by having Lewis Moody at the point of their V-formation response to the haka, and Cowan-Dickie is convinced there will be no complacency against the wounded All Blacks. Borthwick gave the players Monday off before resuming training on Tuesday.

Cowan-Dickie said: “Back then was the semi-final of the World Cup, maybe we left too much emotion out there and didn’t take enough into the final? Could we learn anything from that? Maybe little parts, complacency? Maybe that’s a big one. But the way we trained today, I don’t see any complacency. The boys are as up for it as they were last week.

“It’s a difficult one, I don’t know if we were complacent, it’s just the amount of emotion that went into that semi-final game, did we build the emotions back up for that final? The team we’ve got now is completely different. There are a lot of younger boys involved and they’re frothing at the bit. Obviously Lewis last week added that little bit but, for me, it’s a Test match. If we were playing tomorrow I’d be ready to go.”

Meanwhile, England’s wing sensation Will Joseph has revealed he has been receiving advice from his elder brother, Jonathan – who won 54 caps for his country – after proving Borthwick’s find of the autumn. Joseph won his first cap in 2022 but had to wait four years for a second, in which he scored a record-equalling five tries, earlier this month.

“It’s definitely been a whirlwind, it’s been pretty surreal. I’m quite literally pinching myself,” he said. “It’s very useful having [Jonathan]. I feel like everything I’m going through or experiencing, he definitely would have experienced. He also knows the game inside out, so he’s very supportive. He tells me bits he sees in my game and stuff I can improve on so he’s very useful to have as a brother.”

title: Black Ferns unveil bumper home schedule with regional focus
article_text:
The Black Ferns have announced a bumper home Test schedule for 2027, with three matches set to be played in wider New Zealand regions.

Whitney Hansen’s side will host landmark fixtures between the historic British and Irish Lions side in September 2027, and feature alongside the All Blacks in Brisbane in an Anzac Day double-header with the Wallabies and the Wallaroos.

Trafalgar Park in Nelson, Fraser Park in Timaru, and Palmy Arena in Palmerston North will host the first three Tests of the year, against Canada, USA, and Australia respectively.

Then on September, 4, 2027, the British and Irish Lions will face the Black Ferns XV in Whangarei, kickstarting a five-game tour of New Zealand.

Hansen urges the public to show their support for the side in 2027, especially with such a variety of fixtures hosted by several regions across New Zealand.

“With the first-ever British & Irish Lions Women’s Series coming in 2027, this is a special time for our game,” Hansen said.

“For us, it’s about taking the Black Ferns to places we don’t often get to, connecting with those communities and giving fans the chance to see the team up close in their own backyard. That support will mean a lot to the players heading into a big year.”

Nelson City Council Mayor Nick Smith explained that the region is thrilled to host such a historic fixture against Canada.

“It is simply fantastic for our region to host both Canada, fresh off historic victories over England and ranked third in the world and our very own Black Ferns.

“Having both teams embedded in Nelson for the week and engaging directly with our community makes this much more than a game; it’s a celebration of sport, community pride, and international connection.

“Not only will this match be played right here at Trafalgar Park, but it will also be beamed around the world, showcasing the beauty of our city to a global audience.”

South Canterbury Rugby Chief Executive Tim Hyde-Smith believes hosting the Black Ferns in Timaru will inspire the next generation of players in the region.

“It’s an opportunity to showcase our region to a national and international audience while inspiring the next generation of players, coaches and volunteers throughout our community.”

Manawatu Rugby Union Chief Executive, Doug Tietjens, said the return of several Black Ferns players to their region will be a “significant” moment for Manawatu.

“Having the Black Ferns back in Palmerston North after 28 years is a significant moment for our region. We’re incredibly proud to have four Manawatu players, Kaipo Olsen-Baker, Layla Sae, Elinor-Plum King and Ngano Tavake in the current Black Ferns squad.

“For our young girls to have the opportunity to watch the Black Ferns play here at home, and see players who have come through Manawatu wearing the black jersey, is pretty special.”

April 10: Black Ferns v Canada, Trafalgar Park, Nelson.

April 17: Black Ferns v USA, Fraser Park, Timaru.

August 21: Black Ferns v Wallaroos, Palmy Arena, Palmerston North.

September 4: Black Ferns XV v British and Irish Lions. Semenoff Stadium, Whangarei.

September 11: Black Ferns v Lions. Go Media Stadium, Auckland.

September 14: Invitational XV v Lions. FMG Stadium, Hamilton.

September 18: Black Ferns v Lions. Hnry Stadium, Wellington.

September 25: Black Ferns v Lions. One New Zealand Stadium, Christchurch.

title: Hollie Davidson handed finals role amid online abuse reports
article_text:
World Rugby has confirmed Hollie Davidson will be part of Nations Championship Finals Weekend as rugby fans rally around the Scottish official following reports of online abuse.

Davidson will be back on international duty at Twickenham on Friday, having been named as an assistant referee for Ireland's clash with Australia.

The appointment comes just days after the Scot took charge of France's 45-17 victory over Argentina in Paris.

French sports outlet Sportricolore subsequently took to social media to condemn alleged online harassment directed at Davidson, prompting an outpouring of support from rugby fans.

However, many were keen to draw a line between legitimate criticism and personal abuse.

“Criticism and abuse are two different things, abuse is not needed,” wrote another supporter.

Sadly, this is not the first time Davidson has faced hostility during her refereeing career.

The Scot has previously spoken about the abuse she experienced following a Women's Six Nations encounter between France and England in Bayonne in 2022.

Speaking as the appointments were announced, World Rugby chairman Brett Robinson stressed the importance of supporting referees.

Davidson will work alongside Nika Amashukeli and Christophe Ridley on Friday, while England's Karl Dickson has been handed the biggest game of the weekend.

Dickson will take charge of Sunday's final between France and South Africa.

title: Pumas Roster Changed-up ahead of 2026 Finale vs Scotland
article_text:
A changed-up Pumas roster has been confirmed ahead of the 2026 Finale against Scotland in London. Argentina will be forced into changes to face the Northern British side after injuries and suspensions to players have occurred during the Nations Championship in November.

Loose head prop Mayco Vivas will miss out on facing Scotland. He was red carded against France this past Saturday in Paris. Vivas was Argentina’s replacement loose head yet was on the field very early after Boris Wenger was forced off with a face injury and failed an HIA.

Los Pumas had to change their plans on the fly against Les Bleus. In addition to losing Wenger, Bautista Delguy left the Stade de France with a knee injury inside the opening quarter. Delguy is out of the match against Scotland as is Mateo Carreras who injured his shoulder in the win over Italy in Genoa.

Centurion flanker Pablo Matera was another replacement who will not be available against Scotland. Matera is out of the year-end test match for personal reasons. Meanwhile, center Santiago Chocobares was named to start against France but pulled-out hours before kick-off. He was replaced by Justo Piccardo. Chocbares will miss the Scotland match.

Felipe Contepomi has adjusted to the loss of the aforementioned players. The Pumas head coach has added higher number of six players to his roster. They come in the form of (a) established returning players and (b) fringe players with few or no test caps.

The six players in question are loose head Rodrigo Martínez, hooker Ignacio Ruiz, flanker Santiago Grondona, uncapped fly half Juan Segundo Martín Montilla, center Matías Moroni, and winger Santiago Pernas.

Ruiz is the regular understudy to captain Julián Montoya while Santiago Grondona is also regularly a member of the first-choice 23. Their returns are noteworthy considering the unavailability of Bautista Bernasconi, Marcos Kremer, Pablo Matera, and Joaquín Oviedo.

The inclusion of veteran Matías Moroni could see history made. Moroni played for Los Pumas in Rugby World Cups 2015, 2019 and 2023. He has 99 test caps for his country. If he plays against Scotland then he will become the second Pumas centurion back after Nicolás Sanchez.

Additional history could be made if Matías Medrano or Juan Segundo Martín Montilla receive game time. Medrano is the younger brother of tight head Matías Medrano who has 31 caps and played in Rugby World Cup 2019. Matías Medrano plays loose head and most to Italy this season from Super Rugby Americas.

Matías Medrano and Rodrigo Martínez both arrive with Mayco Vivas and Boris Wegner out. One is certain to play with the doubt being over whether Joel Sclavi will cover tight head or loose head. Sclavi was forced to loose head when Vivas was red carded. He previously played in the left prop position for Los Pumas in 2023.

Juan Segundo Martín Montilla played for the Argentina XV earlier this month against England A. He is from San Juan but moved to Spain with his family at the age of 14 and subsequently to France for rugby. The teenager was named after World Rugby Hall of Famer Juan Martín Hernández. His selection comes ahead of Nicolás Roger who plays for Vannes and it comes following Domingo Miotti’s defection to Italy.

title: Dan Sheehan learns his fate after 'Croc Roll' hearing
article_text:
Ireland’s stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two matches for the croc roll that earned him a red card against South Africa last weekend.

Sheehan, who started at No.8 for the first time in his 42-cap Ireland career in the 20-17 win, was sin-binned for the act of foul play on South Africa’s Marco van Staden, before the yellow card was later upgraded by the Foul Player Review Officer. Van Staden also suffered the same fate after originally being sin-binned for retaliation.

The Foul Play Review Committee met in London on Tuesday and upheld the red card but deemed it worthy of low-entry level sanction.

Sheehan will now miss the Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia at Allianz Stadium on Friday, as well as Leinster’s URC trip to Ospreys in the United Rugby Championship, on 4 December.

The 28-year-old has taken on the responsibility of leading Ireland since regular skipper Caelan Doris was ruled out until the New Year following post-op complications with his knee and foot.

But Tadhg Beirne captained the team in the win over Fiji earlier this month and is the most likely candidate to take on the armband in Sheehan’s enforced absence.

It was only the second time that Beirne had captained Ireland in 76 Tests, but the loose forward has plenty of experience of the role with his province Munster.

title: Sheehan out of Wallabies Test after two-game ban
article_text:
Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan has been banned for two games after a croc-roll tackle against South Africa and will play no part against Australia on Friday night.

The Leinster forward was shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley in the 72nd minute of Ireland's 20-17 victory over the Springboks in Dublin on Saturday.

That was later upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer (FPRO) on the basis of World Rugby's Law 9.20d that "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".

The 28-year-old faced a disciplinary hearing on Monday evening where the panel found that the incident was a "low-entry point" offence and merited a two-week ban.

Sheehan will miss Friday's Nations Championship finals weekend fixture against Australia in Twickenham (20:10 GMT) and Leinster's game against Ospreys in the United Rugby Championship (URC) on 4 December.

Sheehan played at number eight against South Africa, the first time he has started at the position in his Test career.

More usually a hooker, his absence requires another change for Ireland at the base of the scrum for what is their final game of 2026.

Captain Caelan Doris and two-tour British and Irish Lion Jack Conan have missed the entire northern series of the Nations Championship through injury.

Connacht's Sean Jansen deputised in the first game of the November slate against Argentina but a knee injury ruled him out for the remainder of the autumn.

Nick Timoney moved from open-side flanker for the Fiji game before Sheehan was selected to face the back-to-back world champions.

Ireland have an otherwise full squad to choose from for the Wallabies game with head coach Andy Farrell to confirm his selection on Wednesday afternoon (16:00 GMT).

"That was a physical affair, as we knew it was going to be," said assistant coach Andrew Goodman of the victory over South Africa.

"Plenty of excitement and again, looking forward to a massive opportunity for the squad this week. We've got a full squad of fit bodies, which is great."

title: Dan Sheehan ban verdict: Latest disciplinary update
article_text:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan has been handed a two-week ban following his red-card offence during Ireland's 20-17 victory over South Africa on Saturday.

The Ireland hooker will miss Friday's Nations Championship clash with Australia after an independent disciplinary committee upheld his red card.

Sheehan, who started at number eight in Dublin, was sent to the sin bin in the 72nd minute following an on-field review of his crocodile roll on Springboks flanker Marco van Staden.

The South African then retaliated with a dangerous clear-out of his own, which also earned him a yellow card.

Both players subsequently had their yellow cards upgraded to red.

A Foul Play Review Committee, chaired by Philippe Cavalieros (France), alongside Leon Lloyd and Christian Scotland-Williamson (both England), upheld Sheehan's red card.

The committee determined that a two-week suspension was appropriate owing to the low entry point of the offence.

The Ireland international was found to have breached Law 9.20d, which prohibits players from rolling, pulling or twisting an opponent when removing them from the tackle area.

The suspension represents a significant blow for Andy Farrell ahead of Ireland's final international of 2026.

However, Sheehan will be available to return to action for Leinster following the Ospreys fixture, subject to fitness and selection.

Attention now turns to Van Staden's disciplinary verdict, while South Africa are also awaiting further developments surrounding Rassie Erasmus's six-match suspension.

title: All Blacks star Will Jordan stood down with immediate effect
article_text:
New Zealand have suffered a major injury blow ahead of their Nations Championship clash with England, with star outside back Will Jordan ruled out of the tournament's Finals Weekend.

The All Blacks confirmed on Tuesday that Jordan is suffering from a recurring hamstring strain and will play no further part in the international window.

No additional player will be called into the squad to replace him.

The 28-year-old initially suffered the injury against Scotland earlier this month before returning to action against Englandlast weekend.

However, Jordan aggravated the injury during New Zealand's 37-12 defeat at Twickenham.

The news comes as a significant setback for head coach Dave Rennie, with his side looking to bounce back in Saturday's bronze medal clash.

Experienced hooker Samisoni Taukei’aho has joined the New Zealand squad in London as injury cover.

Veteran front-rower Codie Taylor is currently being assessed to determine his availability for Saturday's fixture.

Rennie explained that the additional cover was necessary due to the specialist nature of the hooker position.

Taukei’aho was originally ruled out of the northern hemisphere tour after suffering a calf injury against Australia.

Taylor has not yet been officially ruled out.

- Career highlight: Scored five tries against Tonga in 2021.

- All Blacks record: New Zealand's all-time leading Test try-scorer.

- Other sporting talent: Represented Canterbury in age-grade cricket.

title: Twickenham ‘renamed’ ahead of Nations Championship final
article_text:
Twickenham may be the home of English rugby, but the Springboks are increasingly making it feel like their own.

South Africa have embraced the brilliant nickname ‘Twickersfontein’ ahead of Sunday's Nations Championship final at Allianz Stadium.

The Springboks shared a picture on their official Facebook page of supporters holding a giant green and gold banner reading: “Welcome home to Twickersfontein!”

“The Boks need every possible voice behind them on Sunday,” read the post.

The nickname is particularly fitting given South Africa's remarkable recent record at the home of English rugby.

Sunday will mark the fourth consecutive year in which the Springboks have played a Test against opposition other than England at Twickenham.

Their most recent visit saw them beat Argentina to retain the Rugby Championship title in October 2025.

With a large South African community based in the UK, the Springboks can often count on significant support whenever they play in London.

South Africa have won their last five Tests at the stadium, with their most recent defeat coming against England in November 2021.

The most recent victory saw the Springboks lift the Rugby Championship trophy in front of more than 70,000 supporters.

South Africa have scored 161 points and conceded just 80 across those five victories.

Now, they have the chance to lift another trophy at the same venue.

Twickenham might officially belong to England, but it's easy to see why Springboks supporters have started calling it Twickersfontein.
