title: New Zealand Rugby Union confirms Rennie as national team coach through 2027 World Cup — BBC Sport
article_text:
New Zealand Rugby Union has confirmed that Dave Rennie will remain head coach of the All Blacks through the 2027 World Cup. BBC Sport reports.

Union chief executive Steve Lancaster said that the organization has full confidence in Rennie and that his position is not in question. The union plans to decide in the middle of next year whether the coach will continue working with the national team after the 2027 World Cup.

New Zealand suffered two consecutive defeats in the November part of the Nations Championship. Overall, the All Blacks lost five times during the calendar year — for the first time since 1998.

Rennie took charge of the team in March. In the July Nations Championship matches, the New Zealanders beat France and Ireland, and also defeated the reigning world champions, South Africa, at Ellis Park.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

After the victory over South Africa, New Zealand lost to their opponents three times in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series and lost it 1-3. Two convincing victories over Australia allowed the All Blacks to retain the Bledisloe Cup.

At the same time, the European tour proved difficult: the team lost to Wales for the first time in 73 years and then suffered a crushing defeat to England at Twickenham by a record margin.

The team also experienced the death of long-serving security chief Logan Cadwallader. The BBC notes that the emotional impact of this loss and the demanding schedule of the year are considered factors that partly explain the decline in form. New Zealand rugby administrators will also review the impact of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series as they plan its possible return in 2030.

title: Olympic silver medallist Krissy Scurfield confirms surprise career move
article_text:
Canadian Olympic silver medallist Krissy Scurfield has confirmed an unexpected next step of her career.

In 2027 the 23-year-old will link up with NRLW’s North Queensland Cowboys for one season.

Scurfield made her debut for Canada Sevens as a teenager and was part of the squad that finished second at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, although she did not play in the final after she was hospitalised with a lacerated kidney.

It is expected that Scurfield, who plays wing in the 15-a-side game, will play outside back in rugby league.

“We’re thrilled to welcome Krissy to the Cowboys,” Ricky Henry, Cowboys NRLW head coach, said.

“She’s a highly talented athlete whose success on the international stage speaks for itself.

“Krissy’s desire to test herself in the NRLW highlights her competitive mindset and ambition to keep improving.

“We’re excited to see the positive impact she can have on our squad and the competition.”

During one season with JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club, Loughborough Lightning, Scurfield scored 14 tries in 12 appearances and was included in the league’s 2024/25 Team of the Season.

While with Lightning, the 23-year-old played with current Cowboys full-back Fran Goldthorp, who has represented the Townsville club since 2023.

The Leeds-born back played in all three of England’s Women’s Rugby League World Cup fixtures in October as they exited the tournament at the group stage.

Scurfield is not the first Canadian to have represented an NRLW team, that piece of history is that of Megan Pakulis, and marks an intriguing development in her career.

Scurfield has been named in the Canada Women’s Sevens squad for the opening two legs of the new HSBC SVNS Series season in Dubai and Cape Town.

Canada have been named in Pool B with Fiji, Japan and the Black Ferns Sevens. Last season Canada finished fifth in the SVNS Series and third after three HSBC SVNS World Championship tournaments.

This season a top-four finish will guarantee qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Paris.

title: Poor ticket sales threaten to blight Nations Championship finals opening night
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Sluggish ticket sales look set to blight the first night of the Nations Championship finals at Twickenham this weekend.

Friday’s double-header featuring Italy v Fiji and Ireland v Australia appears on course to be played out in front of a crowd of less than half the stadium’s 82,000 capacity.

The tournament’s official ticket website is showing swathes of tickets still available in most sections with the exception of the top tier, which is expected to be closed.

Officials acknowledged earlier this month that sales could be an issue, with fans having to wait until last weekend to discover the finalised schedule for the three-day showpiece.

Tickets for Saturday’s two games – Wales v Japan and England v New Zealand – are much stronger, and they are also better for Sunday, when Scotland play Argentina before South Africa and France contest the final.

Earlier this month, RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney admitted Twickenham was in “unchartered waters” with regard to the ticket sales for the inaugural tournament, which brings together all the major northern and southern hemisphere nations.

Speaking prior to its opening weekend earlier this month, Sweeney added: “This is the first time we’ve done this.

“A lot of fans are waiting to figure out who is playing who and when. You’ve got to go through those pool matches before you know you you’re playing on finals weekend. It’s a bit like a condensed World Cup.”

title: Nations Championship: 40,000 empty seats on Friday?
article_text:
The first night of the Nations Championship finals could be played in front of some 40,000 empty seats, according to the Guardian. More than half the tickets were still available on Monday for Friday 27 November at Twickenham’s 82,000-capacity Allianz Stadium, and the upper tier is reportedly set to be closed.

That evening, Fiji v Italy opens the programme at 5.40pm (French time), followed by Ireland v Australia, the fifth-place play-off, possibly without Dan Sheehan. Sales are said to be better for the weekend, at 70% of capacity: the organisers hope to fill the stadium on Saturday, for England v All Blacks and Wales v Japan, and on Sunday, the day of France v South Africa, which follows Scotland v Argentina.

Supporters had to wait until the final round of the group stage, on Saturday, to find out which match their team would play, and on which day. Tickets start at £60 on the Friday (£20 for juniors), £100 on the Saturday and £125 on the Sunday (£50 for juniors). A ticket exchange has been opened for supporters who want to follow their team, so the number of empty seats on Friday could rise further still.

The organisers, Six Nations and Sanzaar, declined to comment on sales. Do the maths: 40,000 empty seats out of 82,000 is almost one seat in two. Television audiences are healthier: in England, ITV claims an average of 3 million viewers for its matches, and more than 4 million for Wales’ victory over the All Blacks.

title: Nations Championship reveal match officials for Finals Weekend
article_text:
Englishman Karl Dickson will lead a multi-national team of officials in the inaugural Nations Championship final between France and South Africa on Sunday.

The former Harlequins scrum-half has refereed two Nations Championship fixtures to date, which both ended in wins for France – 42-26 v Australia in July and 54-17 v Fiji in November.

The 44-year-old refereed in his first Rugby World Cup in 2023 and has five Six Nations Championships behind him in the role, with this weekend’s clash the latest headline fixture in an officiating career that began 12 years ago.

Dickson will be assisted on the day by Andrew Brace (Ireland) and James Doleman (New Zealand), with Andrew Jackson (England) as Television Match Official and Richard Kelly (New Zealand) as the Foul Play Review Official.

Nic Berry (Australia) gets the Finals Weekend underway when he takes charge of the sixth place final between Italy and Fiji on Friday, before Nika Amashukeli (Georgia) referees Ireland v Australia in the third place final.

Luke Pearce then oversees the fifth place final between Wales and Japan on Saturday in his first test at Allianz Stadium, with Angus Gardner (Australia) to then referee England v New Zealand in the second place final.

Pierre Brousset (France) will be in the middle for the fourth place final between Scotland and Argentina in the opening match on Sunday, before Dickson referees a test at Allianz Stadium for the first time as France and South Africa battle it out to be the first to lift the Nations Championship trophy.

World Rugby will be supporting its Social Impact Partner, ChildFund Rugby, with visibility across match officials’ jerseys during the Nations Championship.

title: Dave Rennie delivers blunt verdict on All Blacks' Rugby World Cup hopes
article_text:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie remains confident his side has the game plan, coaches, and players to win next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia, despite two worrying defeats to Northern Hemisphere sides in the Nations Championship.

The 62-year-old head coach has come under pressure in the past two weeks, after his side failed to beat Steve Tandy’s Wales in Cardiff, before stumbling against England last weekend to record back-to-back losses for the second time in 2026.

Both the All Blacks and Springboks have recorded several defeats after the brutal seven-game Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series earlier in 2026, as the sides feel the effects of four physical Test matches.

But Rennie, who admitted the group had more than enough reasons to produce a bounce-back performance against England, still believes his side has what it takes to lift the Webb Ellis Cup in Sydney next November.

“Yep,” Rennie said about the All Blacks’ Rugby World Cup prospects.

“We’ve used just about 60 players, so we’ve learnt a lot. Really rapt with the effort from these men, and disappointed with yesterday, but an opportunity to finish strong.

“We’ll have a bit of time through Super Rugby to reassess [the plan]. But we know a lot about these men, and I reckon we’ll be able to put together a really strong squad heading into the international window and then the World Cup.”

While the performance will clearly “hurt” the All Blacks for several weeks, Rennie acknowledged his coaching staff have their work cut out for them to get the players to deliver the necessary response this weekend against England.

“Yeah, it still hurts a lot, and so yeah, it doesn’t matter whether you’re an experienced player or a young player, results and performances like last night hurt.

“We’ve seen that in the group, and to be honest, our job is going to be to get them up and get them up quickly because we’ve got a front again in six days, so we’ll learn our lessons.

“But we’ve got to find a positive way of channelling all that energy into a quality performance on Saturday.”

The All Blacks head coach, who took the role in March, said his side’s effort is there, but the performance was far from accurate enough.

“We get a chance to play England again from a redemption point of view.

“But look, I don’t have an issue with the effort. But we got to be a lot more accurate, and there were so many elements of our game that we didn’t get right last night, and you get dealt to from a good side.

“So yeah, look, we’ve got to be better, but I’m confident that we’ll bounce back.

“We‘re going to [have] be a lot better than we were last night. We defended well for big blocks, and had to defend a lot, and in the end, fell off a fair few tackles compared to England.

“We turned over double the amount of ball that they did, and we had half the amount of possession that they had. So all those things add up to a tough night, but we’re not looking for excuses.”

title: Good news for Steve Borthwick as key England duo get all clear
article_text:
Winger Tommy Freeman has been named in England’s 37-man training squad in preparation for Saturday’s rematch with New Zealand despite missing last weekend’s clash.

The Northampton try machine was pulled out of England’s starting line-up and replaced by Cadan Murley on the eve of the record 37-12 win over the All Blacks after picking up a thigh injury in training. But the injury wasn’t deemed serious enough to rule him out of contention for England’s last Test of the year.

However, Saracens flyer Noah Caluori has been brought into an otherwise settled training group, presumably as a precaution.

Fly-half Fin Smith has also been given the green light to train, having suffered from cramp during Saturday’s match.

Uncapped Harlequins back-rower Jack Kenningham could potentially make his Test debut if head coach Steve Borthwick decides to shake things up for a game that seems suited to experimentation.

Borthwick names his team on Wednesday with a sixth successive Test victory the target as England look to confirm their emergence as World Cup contenders next year.

title: England squad to face New Zealand: Steve Borthwick names 37 players
article_text:
Steve Borthwick has named a 37-man England squad ahead of Saturday's Nations Championship Finals Weekend clash with New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

England return to action on Saturday, 28 November, with kick-off scheduled for 4.40pm and live coverage on ITV1.

The squad has assembled at Pennyhill Park as preparations begin for another meeting with the All Blacks.

Saracens youngster Noah Caluori is included in the 37-man group, having missed the previous training squad.

There are also places for Fin Smith, Ollie Chessum, George Furbank and Seb Atkinson, giving Borthwick plenty of options ahead of his final selection.

Henry Pollock retains his place among the forwards, while George Ford, Marcus Smith and Fin Smith provide competition at fly-half.

England will be hoping to build on their recent 37-12 victory over New Zealand when the sides meet again at Twickenham.

Tickets remain available for Finals Weekend, with each day's ticket providing access to two international matches.

title: Springboks refuse to speak English in press conference after World Rugby ban
article_text:
South Africa assistant coach Mzwandile Stick conducted media duties in the isiXhosa language on Monday.

The Springboks are preparing for their Nations Championship final against France at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Sunday and took the unconventional step of naming their team for the clash early.

And in another unusual turn of events, Stick spoke in the isiXhosa language at the team announcement via an interpreter - a journalist - to communicate with the assembled press pack in London.

It comes a week after head coach Rassie Erasmus was a handed a six-match suspension for comments made in a press conference after their defeat to France in Paris.

Erasmus, 54, questioned whether match officials were involved in "match-fixing" and pointed out numerous decisions he felt were incorrect. You can read more about that here.

The sport's governing body World Rugby acted swiftly and handed the double World Cup winner a ban - which the Springboks have requested a personal hearing for.

There had been suggestions that because English is not Erasmus' first language that his words did not come across as intended. The Springboks appear to have taken the step to allow Stick to speak in isiXhosa to avoid any further misunderstandings.

Stick, who speaks perfect English, has previously answered questions in isiXhosa from South African journalists.

According to the Irish Independent, IsiXhosa is the second most spoken home language in ‌South Africa after isiZulu.

SuperSport journalist Kuhle Sonkosi stepped in to translate Stick's comments about team selection.

“(Stick) used to coach me as an under-21 player and I had been begging him for an opportunity. I never got to play (for the Springboks), ‌so this is my chance to be selected as a translator,” Sonkosi said.

South Africa take on Les Bleus in London on Sunday, with Erasmus once again hosting a watch-along live stream for supporters while banned from attending matches.

title: Rennie gets backing despite All Black defeats
article_text:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of his bosses at New Zealand Rugby to lead the team through to next year's World Cup.

Rennie's side have suffered back-to-back defeats in the November leg of the Nations Championship and have lost five times in the calendar year for the first time since 1998.

"We have complete confidence in Rens," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said.

"His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change."

Rennie was appointed in March and started his All Blacks tenure in style, dispatching France and Ireland in the July part of the Nations Championship before a memorable victory over world champions South Africa in the Springboks' spiritual home of Ellis Park.

But New Zealand lost the next three Tests against the Boks to fall 3-1 in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' [RGR] series, and, although two convincing wins over Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup, the All Blacks have endured a difficult tour of Europe.

A first loss to Wales in 73 years was followed by an English rout in Twickenham, while the All Blacks have also been hit by the tragic death of their long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader.

The emotional toll of Cadwaller's passing along with the arduous schedule this year are thought to be two mitigating factors behind the dip in form, and New Zealand's administrators will review the impact of the RGR series when planning its return in 2030.

Lancaster added that the union will look to make a call in the middle of next year as to whether Rennie takes charge of the team beyond the 2027 World Cup.

"We will conduct a full campaign and season review following this year, as we always do," he said.

"That will inform how we approach next year, but it will also inform our discussions around what the contract situation looks like beyond next year.

"Our intention is to make all those decisions and have clarity before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed from when we appointed Rens earlier this year.

"He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment."

title: South Africa make seven changes for Nations Championship final against France
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

South Africa have made seven changes and one position swap for the Nations Championship final against France at Twickenham on Sunday, with a potential debut off the bench for loose-forward Emmanuel Tshituka.

Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu moved to full-back for the injured Damian Willemse and is replaced at fly-half by Manie Libbok. Cobus Reinach will start at scrum-half.

The rest of the backline remains the same with Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel the centres, and Ethan Hooker and Kurt-Lee Arendse on the wing.

The back row of the scrum is also unchanged with captain Siya Kolisi and Pieter-Steph du Toit the flankers alongside number eight Cameron Hanekom.

Salmaan Moerat comes in at lock alongside Lood de Jager, and there is ‌a new front row of hooker Jan-Hendrik ‌Wessels, and props Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit.

DR Congo-born Tshituka, whose brother Vincent is a Springbok, could debut off the bench, which has a six-two split between forwards and backs.

"We are disappointed in our last two games because we were not as effective as we should have been in a few areas of the game, and that cost us," suspended coach Rassie Erasmus said.

France beat the Springboks 21-19 in Paris in a pool match this month.

South Africa XV: 1 Gerhard Steenekamp, 2 Jan-Hendrik Wessels, 3 Thomas du Toit; 4 Salmaan Moerat, 5 Lood de Jager; 6 Siya Kolisi (captain), 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 8 Cameron Hanekom; 9 Cobus Reinach, 10 Manie Libbok; 11 Ethan Hooker, 12 Damian de Allende, 13 Jesse Kriel, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse; 15 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

Replacements: 16 Malcolm Marx, 17 Ox Nche, 18 Wilco Louw, 19 Eben Etzebeth, 20 Paul de Villiers, 21 Emmanuel Tshituka; 22 Morne van den Berg, 23 Canan Moodie.

title: Springboks duo make World Rugby men’s player of the year shortlist
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Springboks duo Malcolm Marx and Ox Nche have been named on the shortlist for World Rugby’s men’s player of the year.

Marx, last year’s winner, could become the third player to claim the prestigious award in back-to-back seasons, while teammate Nche is bidding to become the first prop to win it.

Marx would join Richie McCaw (who won in 2009 and 2010) and Beauden Barrett (in 2016 and 2017) in an elite group of consecutive winners, as well as Dan Carter and Pieter-Steph du Toit as multiple-time victors.

France and Bordeaux Begles winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey, the Six Nations Player ‌of the Championship in 2026, and New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett complete the shortlist.

France players Fabian Brau-Boirie and Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang have been shortlisted for World Rugby's breakthrough player of the year award, alongside South Africa’s Paul de Villiers and Japan flyhalf Ryunosuke Ito.

New Zealand’s Kaipo Olsen-Baker won the women’s player of the year award last month.

The men’s winners will be announced during the Nations Championship Finals at ‌Twickenham this weekend, with France taking on South Africa in the inaugural showpiece, while England face a rematch against New Zealand after a remarkable thrashing of the All Blacks on Saturday.

Ireland take on Australia, who narrowly squeezed past Wales, with Argentina facing Scotland, Wales playing Japan and Italy facing Fiji.

title: SVNS Series - Dubai 2026 Round 1: Australia 7s vs Argentina 7s Fixture
Rassie Erasmus recalls controversial Springboks star as two players depart
article_text:
The Springboks have made several changes to their squad ahead of the inaugural Nations Championship final against France this weekend.

Rassie Erasmus' side will be looking to put a difficult couple of weeks behind them after suffering consecutive defeats to France and Ireland.

However, despite those setbacks, South Africa still finished top of the southern hemisphere standings after the All Blacks also lost their final two matches against Wales and England.

There have been further setbacks for the world champions, with Erasmus handed a suspension following his criticism of the officiating in the defeat to France.

Meanwhile, Jasper Wiese has also been banned for an illegal clearout at the breakdown.

South Africa will now face France for a second time in a matter of weeks, with the Six Nations champions standing between them and the Nations Championship title.

The final will take place in London on Sunday.

Ahead of the showdown, Erasmus has been forced into a couple of changes to his squad, with two forwards ruled out through injury.

Springbok forwards Ruan Nortje and Ntuthuko Mchunu will return to South Africa after picking up injuries that make them unavailable for selection this weekend.

In response, Erasmus has called up experienced hooker Bongi Mbonambi, who is expected to join the squad in the UK on Tuesday.

The 82-cap international is a two-time Rugby World Cup winner and brings plenty of experience to the group, both on and off the field.

However, his inclusion is unlikely to go unnoticed given his recent controversies.

The hooker had been excluded from training and the Sharks' early URC matches while awaiting the outcome of the investigation. He subsequently departed the Durban-based club with immediate effect to rejoin the Stormers.

He also has a controversial history involving England.

During the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final between England and South Africa in Paris, flanker Tom Curry accused Mbonambi of directing a racial slur at him.

World Rugby launched an investigation but ultimately cleared the Springbok hooker, ruling that there was insufficient evidence to substantiate the allegation.

title: World Rugby Awards 2026 men’s nominees announced
article_text:
The nominees in the men’s categories have been unveiled for the World Rugby Awards 2026, recognising the players and moments that have defined the sport over the past calendar year.

With the women’s categories already presented at the end of the WXV Global Series in October, this year’s men’s shortlist spans three headline categories: International Rugby Players Association Try of the Year, World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year, and Player of the Year in partnership with Visa.

Each nominee for Breakthrough and Player of the Year has been voted by the World Rugby Awards panel, comprised of former legends of the game, Marcelo Bosch, Jacques Burger, Fiona Coghlan, Victor Matfield, Drew Mitchell, Ugo Monye, Kieran Read, Blaine Scully, and Dimitri Yachvili, ensuring that the highest accolades in the sport are a peer recognition reflective of both excellence on the field and inspiration off it.

The Men’s 15s Try of the Year nominees have been selected by members of the International Rugby Players Association, which represents the interests of professional rugby players worldwide. Fans will once again have the final say, voting for their favourite try on World Rugby’s website to decide the winner. Voting closes on Wednesday, 25 November at 17:00 GMT.

The recipients of the World Rugby Awards 2026 men’s categories as well as the Coach of the Year and Rugby for All Awards will be revealed across World Rugby’s digital platforms during the Nations Championship Finals Weekend (27-29 November), ensuring fans everywhere can share in the excitement of the end of the international window. In addition, the highly anticipated World Rugby Men’s 15s Dream Team of the Year will be unveiled on Monday, 30 November, showcasing the standout performers from across the rugby world.

Recognising the most spectacular tries scored on the international stage in 2026, celebrating the skill, creativity and teamwork behind the game’s standout moments. Nominees are:

The five nominees for the International Rugby Players Association Men’s 15s Try of the Year showcase some of the most spectacular attacking rugby of 2026. France captain Antoine Dupont was on the end of a breathtaking attack launched from inside his own 22 against Scotland in the Men's Six Nations, while New Zealand’s Peter Lakai finished a slick Bledisloe Cup move against Australia sparked by Jordie Barrett’s aerial take and Damian McKenzie’s break. England back-row Henry Pollock showed remarkable pace to burst through the Fiji defence and race clear in the Nations Championship, while Pita-Gus Sowakula finished an ambitious, flowing Fiji counter-attack from inside their own half against Wales. Completing the shortlist, Portugal’s Raffaele Storti finished a superb end-to-end team move against Tonga, with Tomás Appleton, Manuel Cardoso Pinto and Samuel Marques combining to send the wing over in the World Rugby Nations Cup.

Recognising emerging talents who have celebrated their first 15s international cap and made a significant impact on the international stage in 2026. Nominees are

The four nominees for World Rugby Men’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year have each made an immediate impact on the international stage in 2026. France centre Fabien Brau-Boirie marked his test debut with a try against Wales in the Men's Six Nations before starting against Italy and all three of France’s July Nations Championship matches, impressing with his ability to make metres through contact and offload in tight spaces. South Africa flanker Paul de Villiers seized his opportunity after being handed a test debut against England, going on to make eight appearances to date for the Springboks and scoring two tries while catching the eye with his work-rate and strength at the breakdown. France wing Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang has successfully made the transition from Olympic gold medallist in sevens to the test arena, scoring twice on debut against Australia and four tries in his first four internationals. Completing the shortlist is Japan fly-half Ryunosuke Itō who was thrust into test rugby before playing a professional match and has quickly established himself with composed performances against Italy, Ireland and France, before scoring his first international try against Australia.

Celebrating the individual who has consistently delivered world‑class performances and inspired fans across the globe during the 2026 international season. Nominees are:

The four nominees for World Rugby Men’s 15s Player of the Year in partnership with Visa reflect outstanding performances across the international game in 2026. New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett has combined his trademark physicality with outstanding distribution, contributing five try assists in ten test starts and helping the All Blacks retain the Bledisloe Cup. France wing Louis Bielle-Biarrey has continued his remarkable try-scoring form, crossing nine times in the Men's Six Nations and 11 times in eight tests to date, while again being named Men's Six Nations Player of the Championship. South Africa prop Ox Nché, shortlisted for a second successive year, has remained a cornerstone of the Springbok pack, featuring throughout their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series victory over New Zealand and scoring his first test try against Australia in Perth. Reigning World Rugby Men’s 15s Player of the Year Malcolm Marx completes the shortlist after another influential season at the heart of the world champions’ forward pack, scoring six tries in 10 tests while remaining a formidable presence at scrum, breakdown and with ball in hand.

title: South Africa win 'sets us up nicely'
article_text:
After Ireland's win over world champions South Africa on Saturday, Andy Farrell had one eye on the past, and another on what is to come.

It was a result that had left Ireland's head coach brimming with pride, as they ended a run of six straight defeats against either the Springboks, New Zealand or France.

With the World Cup now just 10 months away, it is all part of the bigger picture as Ireland aim to progress past the quarter-finals for the first time, with the ultimate goal of lifting the Webb Ellis Cup.

"Whether we lose by three or win by three, you understand how you apply yourself in a big game like that, and it doesn't get any bigger," Farrell said after the 20-17 win.

"You're always trying to kick on to the next level, and sometimes you don't know what that level is because you've never been there as a group.

"But this group is like that. We're trying to do new things together, and it sets us up nicely to keep kicking on."

Farrell looked back to the opening three matches of the Nations Championship in July, when he handed a number of players minutes at international level against Australia and Japan - such as Nick Timoney, Tom Stewart and Tom Clarkson.

Those players played a key role in downing the Springboks in Dublin as second-half replacements.

"We chose to take players to the Southern Hemisphere who had not had that type of experience.

"It's never going to be smelling of roses in that regard [performances over 80 minutes], so you end up where you're at, but we grew as a group, so therefore it's priceless for us."

Given how the tables were weighted, Ireland would have topped the southern hemisphere table by two points.

But the northern hemisphere's domination of the inaugural competition meant a more condensed table, and a fifth-place play-off against Australia will be their reward.

But Friday will be another tough test against a Wallabies side who were one missed penalty away from beating Ireland in Sydney in July.

Speaking before he knew who Ireland would be playing, and when, Farrell denied that playing for fifth place would be an anti-climax.

"You can only deal with what's in front of you," he said.

"We've got another week of international rugby together. We're in the green shirt, and that's special and it's a privilege, so we'll look forward to that."

Ireland's team selection to face South Africa had a surprise as captain Dan Sheehan, who usually plays at hooker, was named to start at number eight.

It was only his second professional start in the back row, with his first outing coming for Leinster against Munster before the international window.

Farrell's decision was certainly justified as Sheehan more than played his role in a scrum that held its own against the world-leading Springbok pack.

"He's so calm, isn't he? I spoke to him over the last couple of weeks about all sorts of things, about number eight, but he wasn't worried and it doesn't bother him in the slightest," said Farrell.

"It's like, 'why are you asking me that question?'. It's almost like an insult. He's so calm, he's such a gifted rugby player.

"That's his character. He just sees it for what it is and he gets on with it. That calm and influence has a knock-on effect that goes through the team."

Another standout for Ireland was Jamison Gibson-Park, whose experience and guile helped the hosts get over the line as the Boks piled on late pressure.

One clearing kick, from his own try line to the halfway line, was a particular standout in a game filled with classy moments.

Farrell described the 34-year-old's kicking as "immense", and said he is getting better with each passing year.

"He got us out of trouble so many times. You almost expect it from him, but you shouldn't," said Farrell.

"He is growing the whole time. I've never seen him in this good of nick, it just shows the hunger that he's got.

"That's what we've got within our group as well, we've got senior players who are constantly working so hard to continue to get better."

title: WRU to discuss Anglo-Welsh move at crucial summit
article_text:
Welsh Rugby Union chief executive (WRU) Abi Tierney says the prospect of Welsh clubs joining an expanded English league will be discussed in January at a crucial two-day summit meeting.

The event, which has been delayed after initially being planned for December, will include the WRU, regions and external stakeholders - with plans to cut a Welsh professional men's side also to be discussed.

"The summit is critical and we're creating it together," said Tierney, speaking after the WRU annual general meeting (AGM) at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

"It is everything. We'll have all the owners and their boards in a room, all the data and facts on the table, and we'll be saying, this is what it tells us."

The WRU announced they hope for both internal and external speakers, with three key areas set to be focused on; financial and commercial, pathways and performance, and what it takes to win.

Tierney admitted the recent prospect of trying to get into an Anglo-Welsh league will be discussed in January.

Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney confirmed earlier in November that the WRU had officially asked to join the English Prem and form an Anglo-Welsh league.

The Prem hopes to expand from 10 to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season, with a "long-term ambition" to grow further.

Prem Rugby has opened a registration process for teams to apply, with a 'request for information stage' now open until 1 February 2027 and which Welsh sides will now consider applying for.

Tierney was careful about what she said as she addressed the issue for the first time.

"Clearly, there's been a significant change in something that wasn't there a year ago that we've got to now take into account," she said.

"When we originally did the consultation last year, Anglo-Welsh wasn't an option. We tested it at the time and were told it wasn't an option.

"We've always said through this process that if other things change and options become available, it's beholden on us to explore all options.

"We've got a lot of water to go under the bridge to figure out what that combination is."

That includes discussions on continued involvement in the United Rugby Championship (URC), the five-country, cross-border competition to which the WRU is committed to providing four sides until 2028.

The WRU are a stakeholder in the competition alongside other member unions from Scotland, Ireland, Italy and South Africa.

"The relationship with the URC continues to be constructive," said Tierney.

"We're talking to them regularly. I think they understand on a human and inter-relational level. We continue to work as we always have."

When asked whether there was any threat of legal action towards the WRU, Tierney replied: "Yes, I think they'll be looking to make sure their interpretation of the contract, that we're clear on that. But we're going through that process."

Whether any Anglo-Welsh involvement affects the number of Welsh men's clubs that are retained remains to be seen.

The WRU has said it intends to drop a professional men's side by 2028.

With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales.

That decision is expected to be made in July 2027 with the summit outlining how the choice will be made.

Tierney was challenged at the AGM on the three-team plan that was unveiled in October 2025, while Ospreys and Scarlets have condemned the plan, saying Welsh rugby should keep four sides.

She responded that the WRU had not heard another plan, although she and director of rugby and head of elite performance Dave Reddin both stated they "were open to other options".

"If you read the consultation documents and responses to the consultation, everybody agreed radical change was needed and the majority agreed reducing the number of clubs," said Tierney.

"It's hard when the impact is real and it becomes one club.

"If you want a consensus, the only thing you're potentially going to have is continuing to do the same thing. I don't think that is going to put Wales on a sustainable footing."

Tierney says she is not giving up on trying to find a solution at the rugby summit.

"We've always said our preference would be to do this via consensus but if we can't get it, that doesn't mean we shouldn't do what we believe is our job as a national governing body," said Tierney.

"To do the right thing for the whole of Welsh rugby, as opposed to what's right for individual parts."

The number of clubs was just one issue that the WRU hierarchy were grilled on, in one of the most robust AGM's in recent memory.

Tierney was asked about whether she thought support would improve in west Wales if a region was cut.

When she suggested concentrating talent and resources could mean more successful clubs that attract support, she was labelled as "naive".

A question was also asked whether there would be more money for each of the three remaining sides.

The four regions currently get £6.5m each from the WRU with £26m given in total.

That overall figure will be reduced by £6m to £20m because of the current financial situation, which means a move to a three-club system will see each organisation having £6.7m each, just £200,000 more than the current amount the four teams get.

title: Ex-NRL flyer opens up on ‘unfinished business’ before SVNS Series return
article_text:
Nathan Lawson has been named in the Australia Men’s Sevens squad for the HSBC SVNS Series opener in Dubai this weekend, returning to the sport with “unfinished business” after a stint with NRL side the St George Illawarra Dragons.

Lawson finished a career-best SVNS season as Australia’s top try-scorer in 2023/24, leading to Olympic honours at the Paris Games. Wallabies winger Mark Nawaqanitawase joined the sevens side before switching to league, with the Aussies falling painfully short of a medal.

Australia were outclassed 31-7 by Fiji at Stade de France, setting up a bronze medal playoff with South Africa. The Blitzboks had finished third in Group A but hit their stride when it mattered most, with Selvyn Davids scoring the match-winner against the Aussies.

Heads dropped as the full-time whistle sounded, echoing throughout the 80,000-seat venue that had hosted the Men’s Rugby World Cup Final less than 12 months earlier. The four-year wait for another shot began, and a lot can happen during that time.

Rugby Australia celebrated the sevens teams, Wallaroos and Wallabies as its night of nights that October, with Lawson recognised as the Shawn Macaky Award winner (Australia Men’s Sevens Player of the Year) before officially sealing a coach switch two months.

The Dragons announced on the eve of Christmas Eve, December 23 that the Olympian had signed on for the 2025 NRL season. Lawson scored three tries against the Manly Sea Eagles in NSW Cup and played a handful of NRL matches, including a double against the Parramatta Eels.

But returning to sevens was always the plan.

“There was always some unfinished business. I was never comfortable leaving. I wanted to push myself out of my comfort zone and do something new,” Lawson told RugbyPass and Rugby.com.au at Rugby Australia.

“But I never really thought that my last tournament in Dubai was mt last. I knew at one point that I wanted to come back.

“I’m grateful that I’ve had the opportunity now to come back and that the program has let me come back. It was a no-brainer for me that I wanted to come back, it was a matter of when and I think it all just fit into place now.”

There had been rumours and reports of Lawson potentially switching codes, but all that became official quite quickly. The Australian started the 2024/25 SVNS Series before linking up with the Dragons, which put the now 27-year-old out of his comfort zone.

Friends had jokingly asked Lawson over the years if he would back himself to play league, but it was never really front of mind. It wasn’t really until the Dragons came knocking that Lawson and his manager asked each other the question: “why not?”

“It really just put me so far out of my comfort zone. I didn’t know how different it was going to be and it’s very different. I had no idea when I first started,” Lawson explained.

“It forced me to learn off all the boys and their system is so professional. The club, the players, their trainings, it was just a good insight into how the other side do it.

“To grow and learn under some big names there, you get a lot of experience and you also just find out how they go about their games.

“I think I picked up a lot and I don’t know much I can bring across here because the game is so different but personal development-wise I’m glad I’ve done and I’m glad I pushed myself but I don’t think that game was for me.”

Lawson has been named in the Australian squad for the SVNS Series season opener in Dubai, with coach Liam Barry selecting four uncapped players as well. USA U20 representative Dane Mitchell could potentially wear green and gold this weekend against the United States.

There has been a lot of change to this squad over the last couple of years, both with playing personnel, the coaching setup, and even the way the team plays. But the core group remains quite similar, with three-time Olympian Henry Hutchison leading the charge.

“I loved playing with the core group of that last team and that’s what stayed together. That’s the only thing that’s kind of stayed the same – the core group.

“The way we play has changed a fair bit. Even the years when I wasn’t here, watching the team really just made me not jealous but I wanted to be out there. Watching them play and the new style of footy they were playing, the skills were so high and it was such a fast-tempo game… it made me want to come back.

“The team was flying last year and hopefully we can bring that on this year. Hopefully I can get the chance to be a part of that.”

title: Steve Borthwick hits rewind button to inspire England’s flying starts
article_text:
Ellis Genge was so fired up by England’s powerful response to the haka on Saturday he stripped off his anthem jacket in the aftermath, completely forgetting he was not starting. Ollie Chessum told Lewis Moody, who had been invited to stand at the point of England’s V formation: “We are going long left, stay on the field and chase the kick-off.” And according to Ben Earl, who would still be out on the Twickenham turf carrying through traffic if he could, some players were so inspired by Moody’s speech the night before they could not sleep.

Against that emotional backdrop, it is small wonder England flew out of the blocks against the All Blacks. Steve Borthwick has spoken a lot about “bringing the fire” recently and on Saturday they torched the place, riding the emotional wave that Moody’s presence inspired from Henry Slade’s fourth-minute try, through to a record victory against New Zealand.

There is more than raw emotion at play here, however. With Borthwick, everything is deliberate, there is always method. In their three matches this month, England have scored the opening try inside the first seven minutes. Go back to the summer and they had their first tries against Fiji and Argentina inside the first five. It is enough of a pattern to make the mind go back to Eddie Jones’s tenure when, midway through the 2019 Six Nations, fast starts had become England’s hallmark.

Back then, England went on a run of scoring inside the first three minutes in five consecutive matches. Jonny May took two minutes to score in the 2019 victory in Dublin that set England on the path to the World Cup final. In Japan, England were still at it – Manu Tuilagi forcing his way over in the semi-final against New Zealand, again after just two minutes. Indeed, between 2018 and 2020, England managed a try inside the first 10 minutes on 16 occasions.

Watching England at the moment you wonder if it is just coincidence that, around the same point of the World Cup cycle, Borthwick’s side are doing similar. Then you remember that Borthwick, who was Jones’s assistant from 2016 to 2020, does not deal in coincidences.

Asked if he has revisited that period under Jones, he said: “Yes, without question. If you look at the scoring rate in first halves and first 20s, all the way through then, through 2019, through to the World Cup, the team was excellent. I’ve revisited session plans, revisited videos of those sessions. I discussed with some people who were around at that point in time. I’ve discussed it with players who were involved at that point. And that meant an adjustment to our training and adjustment to the way we approached [things], and it’s been a very important reference point.”

Borthwick does not pull back the curtain on what England do in training very often so this is quite the level of insight from the head coach. Before his Japan side were thumped by England earlier this month, Jones acknowledged that “the English like to try and blow you out of the water early and then take the game from there”, and he should know, having made it a trademark when he was in charge. His players would talk of detailed walk-throughs and painstaking pre-match analysis, which Borthwick would have been integral to.

“That’s five games in a row now where we have come out and taken the game to the opposition. I want to keep embracing that,” added Borthwick. “We’ve discussed it openly, and discussed it with the senior players. Training is framed in that manner. I’ve talked a lot of times about putting the shirt on and then just wanting to ease into a game, or not wanting to make a mistake. These guys aren’t like that.”

Speak to the senior players Borthwick mentions and it is clear that England’s summer defeat by South Africa, who scored three tries inside the first 11 minutes, was a line in the sand. “Three scores down, it’s extremely hard to come back from that,” said Genge. “In tier-one rugby, to go that many scores down and come back is difficult. It’s definitely the start of Test match rugby that’s the most important.

“Obviously, we were the worst team in the world against South Africa when we got hammered at their gaff. Then we hammered Fiji because of the red [card] apparently and then scraped past Argentina, and then now we’re the best thing since sliced bread.”

It was those opening exchanges against South Africa, then, that convinced Borthwick to go back over video footage, to borrow from Jones’s playbook and overhaul training. The last 20 quarter was, not so long ago, his chief focus, now it is the first 20 minutes. The challenge is backing it up, against New Zealand again this weekend and into next year’s Six Nations, blending the emotion that Borthwick wants with the forensic approach to starting matches, now the watching world is taking note.

“There’s going to be another expectation on us, so again, we’ll take it in our stride,” said Earl. “We don’t think we’re anywhere near the finished product, but we’re bubbling away nicely with almost 12 months to go before the big dance.”

title: 'We're buggered': Sir Graham Henry claims exhaustion factor impacting All Blacks
article_text:
Sir Graham Henry has explained the All Blacks have no “petrol” left in the tank as the gruelling 2026 calendar has taken it’s toll on the squad.

Speaking from London after the All Blacks’ loss to Twickenham, Henry was frank about the state of the squad, calling them “buggered”.

“We just need to be realistic and understand what is going on instead of talking a lot of rubbish half the time,” Henry said on Newstalk ZB’s Mike Hosking talkshow.

“It’s the end of the season and we’re buggered. They’ve just got no gas in the tank, which is unfortunate, but that’s the way it is.”

The All Blacks have played 12 Tests so far in 2026, three in July, four on the tour of South Africa, two Bledisloe Cup fixtures and three more in the November window.

With one game to play, this lines up typically with what the All Blacks play in a calendar year. However, the extra fixtures against South African clubs on the Greatest Rivalry tour added four more games.

Henry claimed it was “too much rugby” but with little left in the tank as they prepare for a rematch with England this weekend.

“Just too much rugby, you know. They’re just running out of petrol, which is really disappointing, but that’s the reality,” Henry repeated.

“They’re a great bunch of guys. I’ve had a lot of association with them this year, and I’m really impressed with the group.

“But, unfortunately, they’re human and they’ve just run out of gas.”

Despite the nature of the loss to England, the third biggest defeat in All Black history, NZR Chief Steve Lancaster has thrown support behind the coaching staff.

“We’re confident that we have the right person coaching this team, no question in our minds,” Lancaster said on RNZ’s Morning Report.

“The team are behind Dave, but they know what they have to achieve.”

title: Australia Sevens dealt major injury blow before HSBC SVNS Series opener
article_text:
Australia have lost a key name ahead of heading to Dubai for the opening leg of the new HSBC SVNS Series season, with news that Mackenzie Davis could be sidelined for up to 12 months with an ACL injury.

Head coach Reg Tayler confirmed the news ahead of the squad announcement, with Rugby Australia Women’s Rookie of the Year Amelia Whitaker set to take Davis’ place in the squad.

Davis played a major part in the Aussie Women’s Sevens claiming the SVNS World Championship title at the back end of the season last year, the 21-year-old also playing in the inaugural season of Ultimate Sevens.

“Devastated, she’s ruptured her ACL,” Tayler said. “We’re hoping for a record time [for her to come back].

“I can’t give you a time frame, I think everyone will see an ACL injury and assume 12 months, it could be 10 months, eight months. We’re going to do everything we can and try and get her back as fast as possible.

“She is a key player for our squad, but we want to set a mentality and I think you would have seen the talent in there at the moment [of] next girl up.

“She’s on board with that, trying to take a bit of a positive out of a negative [headspace]. What can we work on in her rehab process?”

Despite the significant setback, Tayler believes the squad is in a good position, with the team getting around Davis quickly as she begins her journey back to the paddock.

“There’s two girls in there who have ruptured their ACL and done this before,” Tayler added of Davis’ recovery. “It’s not uncommon.

“Just to have people who have experienced it before get around her… she’s a pretty popular member of the squad, she’s still hanging around, she’s been in team meetings.

“We’re going to get her involved as much as we can over the next 12 months during her rehab.”

Davis will have a strong backup in Whitaker, who on top of flourishing in the Next Gen 7s competition earlier this year went on to deliver in XVs, helping the Waratahs secure a seventh Super Rugby Women’s title and enjoy a strong start to her Wallaroos career, earning five caps.

Her breakout season saw her earn the Rugby Australian Women’s Rookie of the Year Award, as well as a nomination for the World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year.

“For us, as an ecosystem, we need to make sure that [we have] a pool of players that we can choose from that are outside our general contracted squad that fit the mould of what we require.

“Other XVs players, we’ve had them in the environment, hopefully we can give them an opportunity to test themselves on the World Series as well. The unique position with the World Series is that the standard is very high, and then there’s not a lot underneath.

“So, we’ve got to make sure that we can give them that.

“With Millie, it’s a bit of a unique case. She’s been in the Sevens pathway as well, she’s played a lot of sevens so it’s not like she’s coming into it for the first time.

“Millie is a really exciting up-and-coming edge player for us, and we think she could be someone who could be knocking down the door in LA.

“To start that journey now is perfect for us.”

title: Three potential debutants named in first All Blacks Sevens squad of season
article_text:
Three potential All Blacks Sevens debutants have been named in the travelling squad for HSBC SVNS Series events in Dubai and Cape Town, while some Olympic silver medallists get their shot back on the world’s premier sevens circuit.

Waisake Salabiau, Brayden Neilson and Grady Forbes are the uncapped prospects selected by coach Willie Rickards to play over the coming weeks, with the season getting underway at Dubai’s The Sevens Stadium on November 28 to 29.

Salabiau has earned higher honours after a captivating NPC season with Waikato, which saw the Fiji-born winger earn a spot in the Hurricanes wider training group. The outside back has been loaned out to the All Blacks Sevens by the Hurricanes.

Two-time Olympian Andrew Knewstubb is another squad member who has linked up with the All Blacks Sevens from a Super Rugby Pacific club’s wider training group. Knewstubb spent last season with the Highlanders but was recently picked up by the Chiefs.

Sione Molia captains a side that also includes Jayden Keelan, Fletcher Morgan, Sofai Notoa-Tipo, Akuila Rokolsioa, Brady Rush, Bradley Tocker and Riley Williams. All Blacks Sevens co-captain Rob Rush has not been named in the first squad of the season.

Five-time World Series [SVNS Series] champion and three-time Olympian Joe Webber is back in the mix, despite New Zealand Sevens celebrating the veteran’s decorated 15-year career on social media earlier this year.

The All Blacks Sevens are the defending Emirates Dubai Sevens champions but will start their title defence in a tough group, drawn in Pool B alongside Spain, traditional rivals Fiji, and 2024 Paris Olympics gold medallists France.

“Our group has come together really well through the preseason and our leaders have set a great example for the new players coming into the environment,” coach Willie Rickards said.

“There’s a sense of excitement about the season and some young players who are ready to make their mark.”

title: Ireland's Dan Sheehan's incident upgraded to red alongside Van Staden
article_text:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan’s yellow card from the 20-17 win over South Africa has been upgraded to a red card offence on Sunday evening, putting the captain in doubt for the last round of the Nations Championship.

Sheehan was sin binned after an on-field review into a “croc roll” clean out on South Africa’s flanker Marco van Staden late in the game in the 72nd minute.

The Bok flanker retaliated with his own act of foul play, a counter-ruck that earned him a yellow card as well.

Van Staden had his card upgraded to red shortly after full time by officials, while Sheehan has now also received an upgrade following post-match review.

Both players will now face judiciary hearings to decide their fate, with potential bans on the table.

Ireland play Australia in the 5th-placed playoff while South Africa have a rematch against France in the inaugural Nations Championship final.

title: Six Nations 2027 fixtures confirmed with historic Scotland first
article_text:
The 2027 Six Nations will feature a historic first, with Scotland set to break a long-standing tradition when the championship returns next February.

For the first time, Scotland will host a Friday-night match in the men's Six Nations, with Ireland travelling to Murrayfield on 5 March.

The match will kick off at 8.10pm, giving Scottish supporters a rare chance to watch their side in championship action under the Friday-night lights.

It is one of several standout fixtures in a tournament that begins with Ireland hosting England and ends with a potential title decider in Dublin.

And with tickets for Scotland's home matches going on sale this week, excitement is already building.

Scotland's meeting with Ireland will be the first Friday-night home fixture in their Six Nations history.

The match takes place on Friday, 5 March, in round four of the championship.

Friday-night rugby is nothing new to the tournament, but Scotland have never previously hosted a Six Nations match in that slot.

Scottish Rugby has confirmed the historic occasion, with the governing body highlighting the significance of the fixture on its official match page.

The clash will also mark Scotland's final home match of the championship.

They begin against Italy on Saturday, 6 February, before welcoming Wales to Murrayfield seven days later.

A trip to France follows, with Ireland visiting Edinburgh after the tournament's only rest weekend.

Scotland then finish their campaign against England at Twickenham, where the Calcutta Cup will be at stake.

Supporters hoping to attend the historic Ireland fixture will soon have their chance.

Scottish Rugby has confirmed that Supporters Club members will receive priority access from Tuesday, 24 November.

Weekend passes go on sale at 10am, followed by individual match tickets at 2pm.

Any remaining tickets will be released for general sale on Thursday, 26 November, at 10am.

The sale covers all three of Scotland's home Six Nations fixtures against Italy, Wales and Ireland.

England face a difficult opening to the 2027 championship.

Steve Borthwick's side travel to Dublin to face Ireland on Friday, 5 February, before welcoming defending champions France to Twickenham on Valentine's Day.

The opening two matches could go a long way towards shaping England's title hopes.

Italy then visit Allianz Stadium on 20 February, before England head to Cardiff to face Wales in round four.

Their campaign concludes with a Calcutta Cup showdown against Scotland on Saturday, 13 March.

With the 2027 Rugby World Cup taking place later in the year, the championship will also provide an important test of England's progress.

The championship begins on Friday, 5 February, and concludes on Saturday, 13 March.

All 15 fixtures have been confirmed, with kick-off times listed below in UK time (GMT).

The championship could deliver a dramatic finish on Saturday, 13 March.

Italy and Wales open Super Saturday in Rome before England host Scotland in the Calcutta Cup.

The final match sees Ireland welcome France to Dublin, with kick-off scheduled for 8.10pm.

If both sides remain in title contention, the championship could be decided under the lights at the Aviva Stadium.

There is also just one rest weekend in the 2027 schedule, rather than the two traditionally used in previous editions.

That means the final two rounds will be played on consecutive weekends.

With a Rugby World Cup looming later in the year, there will be plenty at stake for all six nations.

title: Davis Cup Final 8: Germany and Great Britain Clash for Semifinal Spot
article_text:
The 2026 Davis Cup reaches its end as Germany and Great Britain square off in the quarterfinals of the Final 8 in Bologna. A place in the semifinals against either Austria or Spain is on the line in what promises to be a fiercely contested tie.

World No. 1 Alexander Zverev headlines the German squad as pre-match favorites, but they will face a formidable British side boasting significant depth and world-class doubles pedigree.

Germany punched their ticket to Bologna with a 3-1 victory over Croatia in the second round of qualifying. Zverev proved pivotal by claiming both of his singles rubbers, while the established tandem of Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz delivered in the doubles.

Team captain Michael Kohlmann relies heavily on Zverev at the top of the order, supported by seasoned veterans Jan-Lennard Struff and Yannick Hanfmann. In doubles, the reliable partnership of Krawietz and Puetz provides Germany with one of the most consistent pairings in team tennis.

Great Britain navigated a flawless path to the Final 8, recording back-to-back 4-0 sweeps against Norway and Ecuador. Captain Leon Smith's roster features Arthur Fery, Cameron Norrie, Toby Samuel, Henry Patten, and Neal Skupski.

Fery enters as Britain's leading singles option, complemented by Norrie's extensive top-level experience. The doubles court remains a major weapon for the Brits, with Patten and Skupski offering Grand Slam-caliber credentials. Historically, Germany holds a narrow 6-5 lead in head-to-head Davis Cup meetings, having won their most recent tie 2-1 in 2021.

The quarterfinal clash takes place on Thursday, November 26, at the BolognaFiere Arena, with play scheduled to begin at 4:00 a.m. ET. The match follows the standard best-of-three format, featuring two singles matches followed by a deciding doubles rubber if the score is tied at 1-1.

The opening will pit the lower-ranked singles players against each other, followed by the headline clash between the top seeds, where Zverev is expected to meet Fery. Krawietz and Puetz are slated to face Patten and Skupski in a high-stakes doubles showdown to secure a spot in the final four.

The BolognaFiere Arena hosts the Davis Cup Final 8 from November 24 to 29, serving as the competition's venue for the second consecutive year. Staged on an indoor hard court, the event brings together the eight best nations in the world competing for the prestigious Davis Cup trophy.

title: 'It was ruthless'- GB's Patten on ending top-ranked partnership with Heliovaara
article_text:
Britain's Henry Patten agrees he was "ruthless" in splitting with his doubles partner and close friend Harri Heliovaara, just days after they received the year-end world number one trophy.

Heliovaara and Patten joined forces in 2024 and won Wimbledon together for the second time in July.

In a post on his blog, the Finnish player detailed the disappointment, shock and anger he felt when Patten phoned him with the news.

"I got a lot of stick for calling Harri to tell him," Patten told BBC Sport before Great Britain's Davis Cup quarter-final against Germany.

"I was crumpled over the toilet after the match and Harri, as he often does, had left very quickly to catch a flight back to his family.

"It was ruthless - it was a really difficult decision for me to make for two reasons.

"The first one is we are year-end number ones and we have a great track record together.

"Secondly, me and Harri grew really close during that time. I still consider Harri one of, if not my best friend.

"He's invited to my wedding in the summer. It was probably the first time in my career that I have had to make a decision like that, and I didn't enjoy it."

Patten's new partner will be compatriot Neal Skupski, who says he decided in the space of a "very stressful few hours" to end his pairing with American Christian Harrison.

Patten and Skupski could play their first match as a regular pair against Kevin Krawietz and Tim Putz to decide Britain's quarter-final against Germany on Thursday.

There is little doubt the dust is still settling on a bruising weekend.

"It was a very uncomfortable few hours, but we did speak over the phone for a long time,” Patten continued.

"Obviously I wasn't expecting him to be over the moon about it, and he absolutely has every right to be angry.

"But in that discussion I said I feel like this decision is based on the tennis. I feel that for both of us [it] has stagnated a bit.

"With some time, we'll still remain good friends. That's certainly my hope."

Patten says he has looked up to Skupski for a long time, and enjoys the energy he brings to the court.

He made contact with Ken Skupski, who coaches his brother, last Friday, and did not speak to Neal until he and Harrison had lost in the last four of the ATP Finals the following day.

"It was a very stressful few hours," Skupski recalled.

"After coming off the court, I went to lunch, spoke to [British doubles coach] Louis Cayer, who couldn't really tell me too much as other [British] players are involved.

"It was down to me and my brother to decide what I wanted to do and, at the end of the day, there was only one decision.

"That was the most difficult part - speaking to Christian. We spoke at the hotel, I told him that this opportunity doesn't come along very often to play with another Briton who is a world number one and be able to play Davis Cup and the Olympics in the future.

"So, I think he understood. I don't know if he quite believed me that we hadn't spoken beforehand, but it was two or three hours after the match in which I decided.

"I'm very happy and comfortable with my decision."

The singles in Bologna are likely to feature Arthur Fery and Cameron Norrie and, as British number one, Fery can expect one of the toughest tasks in men's tennis.

The 24-year-old will be up against world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion Alexander Zverev in the second singles match.

Zverev beat Fery in the Wimbledon semi-finals and again at the Vienna Open, with the Briton only winning two games the second time around.

"I've played him a few times already this year, so it's not going to be a completely new thing, which will help me," Fery told BBC Sport earlier in November.

"The serve for me is a challenge because he's close to 2m and I'm on the shorter side of the players out there.

"I struggled to return him, the ball just gets up a lot on me, but I have been working in practice to fight that.

"That's going to serve me not only against Zverev but in general."

Norrie is expected to face Jan-Lennard Struff in the first singles.

The German reached the quarter-finals of Wimbledon and, at 39 in the world, is currently 13 places above Norrie.

Norrie needs little motivation, but the fact Leon Smith is in his last week as captain after over 16 years in the role may help a little.

“I'm so grateful to be here and I think it adds a little bit of motivation to have Leon in our corner. I want to leave it all out there for him,” Norrie added.

“I really like playing with him on the bench there, I feel very relaxed, very chill, he knows when is the right moment to say something.

"He's a great leader and it's a great honour to be in his team."

title: Thomas & Uber Cup Finals 2028 badminton to be hosted in New Delhi
Canada to host BWF World Championships 2027 under Olympics format
article_text:
The next edition of the BWF World Championships will take place in Mississauga, Canada, from July 14-25 in 2027, the Badminton World Federation (BWF) announced on Wednesday.

The latest World Championships were held in New Delhi in August under the 3x21 scoring format.

However, from 2027, just like the World Tour events, the World Championships will also follow the 3x15 scoring system.

The World Championships will adopt a competition format aligned with the Olympics, featuring a group stage followed by a knockout phase across all five disciplines.

The singles events will have 48 players divided into 16 groups of three while the doubles categories will feature 32 pairs divided into eight groups of four.

The top two players or pairs from each group will qualify for the Round of 16.

In an official statement, BWF said, “The new structure guarantees all athletes at least two matches, providing greater competitive opportunities while creating a more engaging tournament across all five disciplines. A maximum of four players or pairs per Member Association may be entered in each event.”

Canada previously played host to the world championships in Calgary in 1985.

The 2027 edition will mark the return of the sport’s flagship individual championship to North America for the first time since Anaheim 2005.

The host cities for the BWF World Championships in 2029 and 2030 will be confirmed later.

title: Sinner 'to MISS Australian Open' as he undergoes surgery after nightmare injury
article_text:
JANNIK SINNER could miss out on next year’s Australian Open after he underwent surgery on his right knee.

Sinner has been dealing with knee pain and has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second time on July 12.

Months of treatment has failed to resolve the issue and surgery and the world No2 revealed on Instagram that he underwent surgery to “improve the condition of my iliotibial band”.

Sinner, 25, posted: “Over the past few months, together with my team we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery.

“After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we’d all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.

“I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team.

“Thank you for all your support. See you soon!”

During his layoff, Sinner lost out on his No1 place to the German Alexander Zverev.

The Australian Open begins on January 17, with the Italian’s injury estimated to keep him out for three to four months.

Sinner has been plagued with health issues, also mentioning that he lost a hefty sum of weight after having his tonsils removed.

This setback is bound to be a mental blow for him after previously stating that the plan was to be fit for the tournament in Melbourne.

Sinner had previously stated: “The goal is to go to Australia, I hope to get there and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand.”

Carlos Alcaraz offered words of encouragement for his fellow tennis competitor after his ATP Finals title win in Turin.

“It’s a shame we don’t have Jannik,” the Spaniard said. “We really miss him.

“I can’t wait to see him fit, healthy. I am pretty sure that he is going to come back even better and stronger.”

While the immediate emotion for the Italian is disappointment, having this surgery and missing out on a trip to Australia will bound to be beneficial for the long-term.

“Right now, however, it is crucial that I take care of my body, because I want to keep playing for another 10 to 15 years.”

title: New Delhi to host 2028 Thomas & Uber Cup badminton
BWF Awards Major Championships Through 2030
article_text:
The Badminton World Federation (BWF) has confirmed several hosts for its BWF Major Championships through to 2030, taking the sport’s flagship tournaments across North America, Asia and Europe.

Beijing was announced host of the BWF Sudirman Cup Finals 2027 last month.

These hosting appointments, along with format changes to the BWF Major Championships, support BWF’s vision to grow badminton’s global reach by bringing its premier tournaments to key and emerging markets.

BWF President Khunying Patama Leeswadtrakul said: “The hosts selected for our Major Championships represent some of the most important and strategic markets in our sport and share our ambition to deliver exceptional events that inspire athletes, engage fans and strengthen badminton’s global profile.

“We look forward to working closely with each host as we continue to elevate our Major Championships and bring badminton’s biggest moments to more people around the world.”

The BWF World Championships 2027 will be held in Mississauga, Canada, from 14-25 July 2027.

The championships will headline a three-tournament North American swing featuring the Canada Open 2027 and US Open 2027 in Los Angeles, showcasing world-class badminton in a key growth market, strengthening the sport’s presence across the region, and building momentum towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

The BWF World Championships 2027 will mark Canada’s second time hosting the event, following Calgary 1985, and the first return of badminton’s flagship individual championship to North America since Anaheim 2005.

President Leeswadtrakul added: “North America is an important growth market for badminton and the 2027 swing represents a major opportunity to build momentum towards LA28 and showcase our sport to new audiences.

“I congratulate Badminton Canada on securing the BWF World Championships 2027. Mississauga will provide an excellent stage for our flagship individual championship and help further strengthen badminton’s presence across the region.”

Further information regarding the BWF Thomas & Uber Cup Finals 2028 in New Delhi, BWF Sudirman Cup Finals 2029 in Korea, and BWF Thomas & Uber Cup Finals 2030 in Paris will be announced in due course.

The host cities for the BWF World Championships in 2029 and 2030 will be confirmed later.

Rinderknech denies refusing doping test
article_text:
French tennis player Arthur Rinderknech says he expects to be exonerated over allegations he refused a doping test.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) confirmed the world number 57 is under investigation, after a report by L'Equipe, external earlier on Wednesday.

It relates to a "surprise" test in June, with French newspaper L'Equipe claiming there was a "possible misunderstanding with the sample collector".

Former Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova is currently serving a four-year ban for refusing to take an out-of-competition doping test in December 2025, and has appealed against the decision.

Rinderknech issued a statement on Instagram in response to L'Equipe's report, saying: "I have already advised the ITIA that I deny the allegation and I have already requested that the matter be heard and determined by an independent tribunal, as is my right."

The 31-year-old, who beat current world number one Alexander Zverev in the first round at Wimbledon last year, believes he will then be "exonerated of the test refusal allegation".

"I have never taken any banned substance and I am proud of my accomplishments in professional tennis, all of which have been achieved through hard work and with integrity always," he added.

The ITIA said the case would be heard by a tribunal early next year and expressed regret that the investigation was first reported by a media outlet.

"We go to great lengths to keep cases confidential, and we are disappointed that the details have become public in this way," an ITIA statement added.
