title: How Jannik Sinner’s injury could affect ATP Rankings with Carlos Alcaraz & Alexander Zverev set to benefit
article_text:
What appeared to be a minor niggle at first now looks to be a serious problem for Jannik Sinner, with the Italian’s injury absence now seemingly set to extend well into 2027.

World No 2 Sinner is reportedly set to undergo surgery in Finland on Tuesday to deal with his ongoing knee injury, with indications that he is dealing with iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS).

Sinner has not played since Wimbledon due to the issue, skipping the US Open and the ATP Finals, among other events, and he now looks likely to miss several more key events next season.

There are indications that Sinner could be out until April next year, a situation that would affect him greatly in the ATP Rankings — and give a big opportunity to Alexander Zverev and Carlos Alcaraz.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

All indications regarding Sinner’s surgery suggest that, at the very least, he will be unable to compete at the Australian Open in January 2027.

The Italian is a two-time champion in Melbourne and was a semi-finalist at the event in 2026, falling to Novak Djokovic in a thrilling five-set encounter.

Assuming that Sinner is unable to play at the Australian Open, he would drop the 800 ranking points he is defending at the event. That would see him fall from 7,950 points to 7,150 points.

That would all but guarantee he loses ground to world No 1 Zverev, who is also defending 800 points following his own semi-final run in Melbourne back in January.

Prior to the Australian Open, the German will drop 40 points from the United Cup, but could win up to 250 points at the Brisbane International instead.

Zverev is effectively guaranteed to remain as the world No 1 post-Australian Open, but could surge to over 11,500 points should he win the title in Melbourne — and potentially sit over 4,000 points ahead of Sinner.

However, assuming he is absent, Sinner could well find himself still ahead of Alcaraz in the ATP Rankings at that point.

Currently 350 points separate world No 2 Sinner and world No 3 Alcaraz, who holds 7,600 points in the ATP Rankings after his triumph at the ATP Finals on Sunday.

The Spaniard is the defending Australian Open champion and has a full 2,000 points to his name from the tournament, meaning his best hope rankings-wise is to defend the title and remain on 7,600 points.

If Sinner was absent, that would see Alcaraz move back to world No 2 post-Melbourne, but any other result for the Spaniard would keep the Italian ahead in the ATP Rankings.

With some suggestions that Sinner could be out for three to four months, all eyes will be on when he returns — and what points he might drop in the mean time.

The Italian will have just 100 points to defend at the Qatar Open in February, though will then have 1,000 points to defend in both Indian Wells and Miami, having completed the ‘Sunshine Double’ back in March of this year.

If Sinner was to also miss these events after also missing the Australian Open, he would lose a further 2,100 points and drop to 5,050 points in the ATP Rankings.

Hypothetically, that would see him drop further behind both Alcaraz and Zverev, and both men would have the chance to surge ahead of the Italian significantly.

Across that same stretch, Zverev has just 50 points to defend at the Acapulco Open, and then 400 points each at both Indian Wells and the Miami Open, a total of 850 points that is 1,250 points less than Sinner’s equivalent.

Meanwhile, Alcaraz will have 500 points to defend as the reigning Qatar Open champion in February, but then just 400 points in Indian Wells and a mere 50 points at the Miami Open.

Obviously, Sinner will have a notable chance to gain points across the second half of the season, having not played since Wimbledon this year. He also has just 50 points to defend at the French Open, following his shock exit in round two in May.

However, there is no denying that if his injury is as serious as feared, he could find himself trailing both Zverev and Alcaraz significantly when he returns.

title: Jannik Sinner to reportedly undergo knee surgery, will miss second straight Grand Slam
article_text:
Former World No. 1 Jannik Sinner is set to undergo surgery this week for the right knee injury that ended his 2026 season, Sky Sport Italy reported Monday.

The recovery is expected to take three-to-four months, which will keep the five-time major champion out of the Australian Open. It will be Sinner's second consecutive Grand Slam absence. He withdrew from the US Open with the same injury.

That prevented Sinner from advancing to the US Open final for the third consecutive year. He won the tournament in 2024, defeating American Taylor Fritz. Last year, he finished as runner-up, losing to rival Carlos Alcaraz.

Sinner also withdrew from the Cincinnati Open in August due to his knee injury. With that event taking place so close to the US Open, his availability to play in Queens was put in doubt.

However, Sinner not playing in Cincinnati was viewed as a precautionary measure that would allow him an opportunity to recover and train for the US Open. But Sinner's knee turned out to need more treatment than originally anticipated.

Sinner, 25, won his second consecutive Wimbledon title approximately a month earlier, defeating Alexander Zverev in the final. But he didn't play in an event since that July 12 match.

The surgery will cap off a difficult year for Sinner. Though he did win Wimbledon, Sinner lost to Novak Djokovic in the Australian Open semifinals and was upset by Juan Manuel Cerundolo in the second round of the French Open while struggling with dehydration and cramping.

In a video posted to social media, Sinner told fans that he needed to think about his long-term career when he decided to end his 2026 season in October. At the time, he said he and his doctors had mapped out a course of treatment. Apparently, Sinner's right knee didn't respond to that regiment. Or surgery was always the eventual outcome.

"I will do everything possible to get back to 100 percent," Sinner said in the video. "I will thank you already in advance for your support and hope to see you very, very soon on court again. Ciao, Ciao."

At the Davis Cup Finals this week in Bologna, Italy, Italian team captain Filippo Volandri told reporters that he sent a message of support to Sinner.

"We wish him the best of luck because he's important not only for the Davis Cup, but for Italy and for everyone," Volandri said, via Sky Sport Italy. "Regardless of whether he's not here physically, he's here because he writes to us in our chat. We wish him the best of luck and are waiting for him with open arms."

title: Blockbuster Coco Gauff doubles partnership teased by Taylor Townsend ahead of LA 2028 Olympic Games
article_text:
Taylor Townsend has revealed that she and Coco Gauff intend to pair up and go for gold in the women’s doubles event at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

It is now only a year and a half until the Summer Olympics head to Los Angeles, in what will be a home games for Townsend, Gauff, and the rest of the potential US tennis squad.

Both Gauff and Townsend represented their country in the Billie Jean King Cup this past weekend, with the USA easing their way to a 4-0 victory over Hungary to progress to next year’s qualifiers.

The USA were 2-0 up after a strong Saturday, with Gauff defeating Dalma Galfi and Ann Li beating Anna Bondar in the opening women’s singles rubbers in Florida.

World No 4 Gauff and Townsend then paired up for the women’s doubles and sealed the decisive victory on Sunday, defeating Galfi and Bondar 6-4, 6-3 before Ashlyn Krueger saw off Adrienn Nagy in a dead rubber.

Victory for Townsend saw her cap off a stunning year on the doubles court, completing the Career Grand Slam alongside Katerina Siniakova thanks to triumphs at the French Open and US Open, as well as claiming victory at the WTA Finals.

With Townsend and Czech Siniakova unable to play together at the Olympics, it now appears that the doubles world No 2 will be pairing up with Gauff for their home games.

Speaking in press after the USA’s victory, Townsend teased that she and Gauff had begun the process of developing their partnership ahead of LA 2028.

She said: “The only thing that was going through my mind, honestly, is like I hope these people are enjoying [this] because this is the partnership for 2028 Olympics, so you know they’re getting a chance to be able to see a sneak peek.

“Hopefully we’ll have some more opportunities to be on the same side of the net with each other because I always really enjoy it.”

A two-time Grand Slam singles champion, Gauff is also a hugely accomplished doubles player. Much like Townsend, she is a former doubles world No 1, and she won the 2024 French Open doubles title alongside Siniakova.

Speaking after her victory alongside Townsend this weekend, she opened up about how playing with her compatriot was an enjoyable experience.

“The few times that we have played, playing with Taylor has been so fun. She has a unique skill of being able to uplift you on court,” added the 21-year-old.

“She is already one of the greats and will definitely go down as one of the greats, so being able to learn from and play with her has been so fun.”

Gauff previously competed at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, when she memorably got to be the USA flagbearer at the opening ceremony alongside Lebron James.

However, she was unable to claim a medal, falling in the third round of the women’s singles, the second round of the women’s doubles alongside Jessica Pegula, and the quarter-final of the mixed doubles alongside Taylor Fritz.

Townsend has never previously competed at the Olympics, with the 30-year-old potentially in line to make her debut at the prestigious event.

The USA will be eligible to achieve up to 12 quota places for LA 2028, which would include four spots in both the men’s and women’s singles, as well as two pairings in both the men’s and women’s doubles, and one pairing for mixed doubles.

title: Alexander Zverev sets unfortunate year-end No 1 record despite winning two Grand Slam titles
article_text:
The 2026 ATP Tour season is officially over, and it is Alexander Zverev who sits at the top of the world rankings after a career-defining year for the German.

Heading into 2026, Zverev was one of the greatest ‘nearly men’ of the sport, falling in three Grand Slam finals despite winning an array of Masters 1000 titles, two ATP Finals, and Olympic gold back in 2021.

However, the 29-year-old’s fortunes at the majors improved dramatically over the past twelve months, with the German battling his way to a first Grand Slam title at the French Open in June, beating Flavio Cobolli in the final.

That was then followed by a second major triumph later in the season, with Zverev defeating Ben Shelton in four sets to lift the US Open title in Septmeber.

Those results helped Zverev debut as the world No 1 earlier this month, and also helped him seal the year-end No 1 ranking ahead of Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz.

However, despite breaking new ground in 2026, Zverev has now set a rather unfortunate record in the ATP Rankings.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Outside of his victories at Roland Garros and the US Open, Zverev was also the runner-up to Sinner at both Wimbledon and the Madrid Open in 2026. He was also a beaten finalist at the ATP Finals this past week, falling to Alcaraz in the championship match.

Though he tasted success at two Grand Slam tournaments, they proved to be the only titles that the 29-year-old won across the season, and that is now the least amount of titles won in a year by the ATP’s year-end No 1 since the ATP Rankings first launched in 1973.

Prior to Zverev, the record for the least number of titles won by a year-end No 1 was four, jointly held by Novak Djokovic (2018 and 2020), Rafael Nadal (2019), Roger Federer (2009), and Pete Sampras (1998).

The record for the most titles won by a year-end No 1 was set in the very first year of the ATP Rankings, with Ilie Nastase — the first No 1 in ATP history — winning a staggering 16 tour-level titles in 1973.

The two players with the most singles titles won on the ATP Tour in 2026 are world No 2 Sinner and world No 3 Alcaraz, who both won six titles across the year.

Zverev was able to finish the season as the year-end No 1 ahead of both men in part due to his consistency at the Grand Slam tournaments. He banked 2,000 points at both the French Open and US Open, 1,300 points for reaching the Wimbledon final, and 800 points for reaching the semi-final of the Australian Open.

That means Zverev earned 6,100 ranking points from the Grand Slams this year, contributing to his overall total of 10,350 points for the season.

While Zverev banked consistent points across the four majors, Sinner and Alcaraz did not. World No 2 Sinner won Wimbledon and reached the last four of the Australian Open, though lost in round two of the French Open and missed every tournament post-Wimbledon due to injury — including the US Open.

Meanwhile, Alcaraz lifted the Australian Open title in January and was a quarter-finalist at the US Open, though four and a half months out with injury saw him miss both the French Open and Wimbledon, alongside a string of further tournaments.

Ultimately this record is not entirely Zverev’s fault, with the rankings system and injuries to two of his main rivals not exactly in his control.

However, the German will likely have to win more titles in 2027 if he wants to hold on to his world No 1 ranking.

title: Jannik Sinner’s estimated recovery timeline from knee surgery revealed – report
article_text:
With Jannik Sinner reportedly set to undergo surgery on his knee, the world No 2’s lengthy absence from the tour looks likely to extend beyond the start of 2027.

A right knee injury has prevented Sinner from playing since he defeated Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final in July.

Sinner has not shared details about the specific nature of his knee injury, but it has been reported that the issue he is dealing with is iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS).

Earlier today, Italian newspaper Il Messaggero reported Sinner was set to travel to Finland for an operation on his right knee on Tuesday.

Graziano Urbani, who wrote the article, claimed Sinner’s surgery will rule him out of the 2027 Australian Open.

“This decision inevitably alters the Italian’s plans and extends his recovery timeline: Sinner will not participate in the Australian Open,” Urbani wrote (translated from Italian).

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

“The goal of returning to action in Australia — a prospect he had been working toward over the last few weeks — has therefore definitively slipped out of reach.”

Angelo Mangiante, a journalist for Sky Sport Italy, confirmed the news about Sinner’s decision to undergo surgery.

“He will be operated on by surgeon Lasse Lempainen, an orthopaedic specialist of international renown considered one of the world’s leading experts in tendon and muscle injuries,” Mangiante wrote on Twitter/X.

“The surgery will take place in Turku, where Jannik will arrive today. The condition, as is well known, is tendinopathy on the outside of the right knee, known as iliotibial band syndrome.”

On Sinner’s estimated recovery timeline, Mangiante added: “Recovery is estimated to take 3-4 months, so he could return for the clay-court season after the American tournaments. But that is obviously just a possibility.”

Earlier this month, Sinner divulged he was hoping to make his comeback in time to play the 2027 Australian Open.

“The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” said the five-time Grand Slam champion.

Sinner won the first five Masters 1000 tournaments in 2026 before he defended his Wimbledon title.

title: Emma Raducanu Joins Uniqlo’s Commitment to Keep U.K. Families Warm This Winter
article_text:
LONDON — U.S. Open champion Emma Raducanu joined Uniqlo’s charitable effort to support families facing hardship in the U.K.

The Uniqlo global brand ambassador visited Little Village in Camden, where she met families, staff and volunteers, just as the retailer marked its donation of 16,800 Heattech items to 29 baby banks this year.

The visit, held around World Children’s Day on Nov. 20, was part of the retailer’s Heart of LifeWear initiative and its ongoing partnership with Save the Children.

During her visit the brand said Raducanu spoke with a mother and her 4-year-old daughter about the support they had received from the baby bank. She also helped volunteers pack personalized bundles, which included Heattech clothing donated by Uniqlo alongside hygiene products, baby equipment, toys and books.

“Today has been a chance to see how the program can make a genuine difference to families, and how everyday clothing like Heattech can bring warmth, comfort and support when it is needed most,” Raducanu said.

The U.K. donation forms part of a broader effort across Europe. The fashion label under Fast Retailing has vowed to donate more than 100,000 Heattech items to charities for the third consecutive winter.

Save the Children has partnered with Uniqlo globally for more than four years. In Europe, the partnership has expanded over the past three years through fundraising, product donations and local initiatives.

The charity is a founding member of the Baby Bank Alliance, a network of more than 270 baby banks in the U.K. that provide families with essentials free of charge. In 2025, baby banks supported 210,000 families and 400,000 children.

As reported, Uniqlo named Raducanu its latest global brand ambassador earlier this year. The British tennis player joins a roster that includes Roger Federer, Kei Nishikori, Adam Scott and Ayumu Hirano. Raducanu is the roster’s only woman and its fifth tennis player.

The appointment is intended to extend beyond the court. Uniqlo has developed an initial tennis dress for Raducanu, but she will also wear and represent the brand off court, reflecting the brand’s LifeWear positioning around clothing for different parts of everyday life.

Clare Waight Keller, Uniqlo’s creative director, said the company had long wanted a woman athlete on its ambassador team. She described Raducanu as an exciting choice for connecting with younger customers and aspiring athletes.

“The way Emma conducts herself, and her confidence, but addressing struggles too — I think a lot of young people do struggle — and so the nice balance for us is that it feels very authentic and very real, and that’s what we love so much,” Waight Keller added.

title: Syed Modi: Depth of Home Talent in Focus
article_text:
The next generation of India’s women’s singles shuttlers take centrestage with the Syed Modi India International 2026 beginning Tuesday in Lucknow.

While Indian icon Pusarla V Sindhu won’t be in action, several of those seeking to follow in her footsteps will be geared up for what promises to be an intense week. India have nine women’s singles players in the top 50; apart from Pusarla, the others are in action in Lucknow.

Among those evoking interest will be world No.47 Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj, who was relatively unknown until a week ago. That changed in the space of two days at last week’s LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 when she first took down Mia Blichfeldt, followed by the even bigger upset of Chen Yu Fei. Ramraj is in the top quarter, and will expect to run into top seed Riko Gunji in the second round.

Among other Indian prospects are second seed and world No.21 Tanvi Sharma, winner of the YONEX Taipei Open; No.23 Unnati Hooda, winner of the Polish Open; VICTOR Korea Masters winner Ashmita Chaliha, and Thailand Masters winner Devika Sihag.

Then there are other prospects like Isharani Baruah, Anmol Kharb, Malvika Bansod and Shriyanshi Valishetty, among others, who have had some memorable performances this season.

Tanvi Patri, who fell in a dramatic final at the Youth Olympics recently, will play the qualifying draw.

In men’s singles, second seed Lee Zii Jia will draw the most attention, particularly after he made the semifinals of the CLASH OF CLANS Arctic Open 2026.

Teh Jia Heng heads the draw; for home fans, No.3 seed HS Prannoy and eighth seed Tarun Mannepalli will shoulder the hopes of home fans.

title: Alex Eala’s return to WTA Tour event confirmed as 2027 schedule begins to take shape
article_text:
Alex Eala’s schedule for the 2027 WTA Tour season continues to take shape, with the Filipina confirmed for a return to the Abu Dhabi Open next season.

The Abu Dhabi Open will take place from January 30th to February 6th 2027, and currently looks set to be Eala’s third event of the season.

World No 15 Eala is already confirmed to be starting her season at the Auckland Open in early January, where she will look to better this year’s run to the semi-final, before competing at the Australian Open — the opening Grand Slam tournament of 2027.

The WTA 500 event in Abu Dhabi will take place directly after the Australian Open, with Eala reaching the quarter-final of the tournament on her second event appearance this past February.

The Filipina defeated Zeynep Sonmez and Aliaksandra Sasnovich to reach the last eight before losing to second seed Ekaterina Alexandrova, the eventual runner-up.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Eala had previously received a wildcard into the tournament while still a teenager back in 2024, losing to Magda Linette in the opening round.

With the tournament sharing a sponsor with the Washington Open, the tournament Eala memorably won this summer, all eyes will be on whether she can achieve a similar level of success.

In a statement, Eala said: “Returning to Abu Dhabi for my third Mubadala Abu Dhabi Open is something I’m really looking forward to, especially as they celebrate the tournament’s fifth anniversary.

“The energy from the Filipino community and the fans across the UAE makes competing here that much more special. I’ve continued to grow and develop myself as a player, and I’m excited to bring that experience back to Abu Dhabi this year on my favourite surface on tour. It’s always a privilege to compete alongside such a talented field and in front of such energetic crowds.

“The crowds that came and watched me last year were electric and it was an event I loved participating in. After the triumph at the Mubadala DC Open this summer, hopefully I can bring the same luck with me in the UAE capital.”

So far, she is the only player confirmed for the Abu Dhabi Open field, though the tournament traditionally attracts high-profile players. Aryna Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina, and Belinda Bencic have all won the title since the event was first launched in 2021.

Sara Bejlek won the title in 2026, beating Alexandrova in the final.

The Abu Dhabi Open will likely be the first of three events for Eala in the Middle East Swing, with the first two WTA 1000 events of the year also held in February.

Following the Abu Dhabi Open, the first WTA 1000 event of the year will be the Qatar Ladies Open in Doha, which will itself then be followed by the second WTA 1000 event of the season at the Dubai Tennis Championships.

Eala will be targeting a strong campaign after a career-best year, cracking the top 20 for the first time and ending the season at a new high of 15th in the WTA Rankings.

title: Denmark claim only European title as Korea and Chinese Taipei dominate Scottish Open
article_text:
Europe had several finalists at the Scottish Open, but Kristoffer Kolding/Mette Werge were the only Europeans to leave with a title as Korea and Chinese Taipei claimed the remaining four.

Kolding/Werge (3) secured the mixed doubles title in an all-Danish final against compatriots Jesper Toft/Amalie Cecilie Kudsk, winning 21-19 13-21 25-23.

Germany also had two pairs in the finals. Stine Küspert/Isabel Lohau finished runners-up in women's doubles, while Daniel Hess/Simon Krax reached the men's doubles final. Both pairs were beaten by Korean opposition, with Seung Hee Lee/Park Min Ji winning 21-17 21-16 and Jin Sung Ik/Lee Hyeong Woo taking the title 14-21 22-20 21-7.

Croatia's Aria Dinata also reached the men's singles final, but Chinese Taipei's Ting Yen-Chen proved too strong, winning 21-9 21-14.

Korea collected three titles in total, with Kim Min Ji also winning the women's singles final against compatriot Park Ga Eun 20-22 22-20 21-19.

The Scottish Open therefore ended with three titles for Korea, one for Chinese Taipei and one for Denmark, the sole European winner of the tournament.

title: How Lakshya Sen turned a faltering season into a World Tour Finals comeback
article_text:
Written off after a string of early defeats, Lakshya Sen won 13 straight matches in November, picked up two Super 500 titles and booked his first World Tour Finals berth in five years.

Lakshya Sen lost the opening game of the Kumamoto Masters Japan final 13-21 to Koki Watanabe, a home favourite who had already beaten him twice this year.

Sixty-four minutes later, he had turned it around, winning 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 to become the first Indian to lift the title since the tournament was introduced in 2023. It was his second Super 500 crown in a fortnight.

A month earlier, such a run would have seemed improbable.

Lakshya had entered the final stretch of the season on the back of first-round exits at the China Masters and Denmark Open, a second-round exit at the Asian Games and an upset defeat at the home World Championships.

The question then was not whether he could win titles, but whether he could string together wins.

The year had promised much more. At the All England Open in March, Lakshya beat top seed and defending champion Shi Yu Qi 23-21, 19-21, 21-18 in the first round, ending a five-match losing streak against the Chinese shuttler.

He then survived a four-match-point deficit against Ng Ka Long Angus to win 21-19, 21-23, 21-10, beat Li Shi Feng 21-13, 21-16 in the quarter-finals and defeated Canada's Victor Lai to reach his second All England final.

Lin Chun-Yi beat him 15-21, 20-22 in the title match, extending his losing streak against the Taiwanese shuttler to five.

By late May, Lakshya had returned to the world top 10 for the first time in more than 440 days.

Lakshya injured his elbow in the opening game of India's Thomas Cup quarter-final against Chou Tien-chen, although he went on to win 18-21, 22-20, 21-17 as India secured bronze.

Defeats to Watanabe followed at the Singapore Open and Japan Open.

At the World Championships in New Delhi in August, he won the opening game 21-19 against world No. 92 Garret Tan, an 18-year-old American, before losing in three games.

Victor Lai, whom he had beaten in the All England semi-finals, knocked him out of the China Masters in straight games. At the Asian Games, Lakshya led Loh Kean Yew 5-1 in the opening game before losing 12-21, 21-15, 14-21 in the second round.

Chou then beat him 18-21, 21-13, 15-21 in the opening round of the Denmark Open.

Lakshya arrived at the Hylo Open in Saarbrucken as the seventh seed.

He dropped the opening game against Finland's Kalle Koljonen in the quarter-finals before rallying to win 14-21, 21-17, 21-13. He then beat world No. 14 Toma Junior Popov 21-17, 21-13 in the semi-finals.

In the final, he faced fourth seed and defending champion Jonatan Christie, who held a 4-3 lead in their head-to-head record. Lakshya won 21-17, 21-10 in 39 minutes to level the record and claim his first title since the Australian Open in November 2025.

It was his second Hylo Open title, following his 2019 triumph, and came on the same day PV Sindhu won the women's singles. "Approach remains the same," Lakshya said afterwards, crediting his family, coaches and support team.

Seeded eighth in Kumamoto, Lakshya recovered from 12-16 down in the opening game against Chi Yu Jen to win his first-round match before beating China's Dong Tianyao to reach the quarter-finals.

There, he defeated Yushi Tanaka, his opponent in last year's Australian Open final, 21-16, 21-15.

The semi-final against Indonesia's world No. 10 Alwi Farhan went the distance. Lakshya took the opening game 21-12 but lost the second 15-21 after Farhan opened up an 11-4 lead at the interval. He then closed out the decider 21-11 in 70 minutes.

A year earlier, his Kumamoto campaign had ended in the semi-finals against Kenta Nishimoto.

The final against Watanabe carried added significance in the race for the World Tour Finals.

Lakshya was 10th in the Race to Finals before the tournament. The title, worth 9,200 points, lifted him to sixth and brought him within touching distance of qualification for Hangzhou.

The Hong Kong Open was the final tournament in the qualifying window.

Lakshya needed a semi-final finish to secure his place, but the equation eased on the opening day when Kidambi Srikanth beat Watanabe in the first round.

Lakshya entered the week with 74,180 points, compared to Watanabe's 73,620.

After beating home player Lee Cheuk Yiu in the opening round, he defeated Denmark's Rasmus Gemke 21-11, 21-18 and then eighth seed Loh 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 in the quarter-finals, avenging his Asian Games defeat.

It was his 13th consecutive win across three tournaments.

The streak ended in the semi-finals against third seed Anders Antonsen, who beat him 13-21, 13-21.

Antonsen went on to win the title by walkover after Kunlavut Vitidsarn withdrew from the final with a back injury.

The clearest difference has been Lakshya's ability to navigate close matches.

Through the middle of the year, he lost deciding games to Tan, Loh and Chou. In November, he came from a game down against Koljonen and Watanabe, while also winning three-game matches against Farhan and Loh.

His long-time mentor Vimal Kumar credited the coaching team's planning after Kumamoto, writing on X that the win over Watanabe brought back "memories of the brilliance he displayed in 2021-22".

That period saw Lakshya reach a career-high world No. 6 in November 2022. He currently sits at No. 11.

title: French pair target Grand Slam glory after ATP Finals crown in Turin
article_text:
French tennis players Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti were on Monday setting their sights on playing in their country's Davis Cup team and trophies at the four Grand Slam tournaments next year after capturing the doubles title at the 2026 men's end-of-season championships.

Arribagé and Olivetti beat the fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic 3-6, 7-6, 10-6 in Turin on Sunday night to claim their most prestigious prize since teaming up in October 2025.

"The main objectives for next season will be the French [Davis Cup] team and winning Grand Slams," Arribagé said.

"Following on from what we have done this year, we want to perform better but without setting ourselves limits," he added.

Arribagé, 26, and Olivetti, 34, went into the eight-team doubles event in Italy as the sixth seeds on the back of crowns in Auckland, Dallas, Montpellier, Halle, Mallorca and Basel as well as finals in Munich, Tokyo and Lyon.

On 15 November, they lost to Arevalo and Pavic in straight sets in the opening match of the round robin stage.

Two days later, they bounced back with a 6-4, 7-6 victory over the eighth seeds Orlando Luz and Rafael Matos. On 19 November, they upset the top seeds Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara to advance to the semi-finals.

There, they squandered three match points and then saved three match points on their way to a 7-6, 6-7, 12-10 win over the seventh seeds Kevin Krawietz et Tim Pütz.

"After we won in Auckland I started to feel that we could really be a very solid pair," added Arribagé. "And I felt that we could achieve some great things if we worked hard.

"We're the pair that has won the most tournaments this year but we were missing that big title. With this trophy, there is no better way to end the season."

Arribagé and Olivetti are the third all-French pair after Fabrice Santoro and Michaël Llodra and Nicolas Mahut and Pierre-Hugues Herbert to win the doubles title at the end of season championships since it was set up in 1970.

In the singles event, Carlos Alcaraz capped his return from a five-month injury lay-off with a third consecutive title and a first ATP Finals trophy.

The Spaniard overwhelmed the top seed Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 on Sunday night to join André Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic as the only men to win at the four Grand Slam venues in Melbourne, Paris, London and New York as well as the end-of-year championships.

"This one is special," Alcaraz said. "This one means the world to me, to my team, to my family. They know how hard I've been chasing this moment and how hard I've been working to lift this trophy."

Alcaraz dispatched seventh seed Frances Tiafoe, fourth seed Daniil Medvedev and fifth seed Flavio Cobolli with dropping a set during the round robin stage.

He dropped the opening set to third seed Ben Shelton before recovering to win 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 in the semi-finals on Saturday.

Zverev, who won the end-of-season championhips in 2018 and 2021, was munificent in defeat.

"You're an absolute legend of our sport and you are only 23-years-old," said the 29-year-old German during the trophy presentation ceremony. "So if you retire tomorrow, it's okay. You can relax!"

title: Carlos Alcaraz makes Davis Cup Finals decision as he gives injury update after ATP Finals victory
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has confirmed whether he is still planning to play at the 2026 Davis Cup Finals after his maiden triumph at the ATP Finals.

The seven-time major champion prevailed 6-2, 7-6(7) against world No 1 Alexander Zverev in the final at the season-ending championships in Turin.

At the age of 23, Alcaraz has become the youngest player in history to win the ATP Finals and all four Grand Slam tournaments.

Alcaraz secured the title in Turin with a perfect 5-0 record despite suffering a left hamstring injury in his second round robin match against Daniil Medvedev.

After the final, Alcaraz revealed he is planning to lead his country at the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna this week.

“I’m really looking forward to trying to complete the tournaments I have left,” the world No 3 said in his Spanish press conference.

“The Davis Cup is something very important to me. I’ll try to get to Bologna as ready as possible physically. It’s going to be a very, very nice week, and one I’m really looking forward to.”

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

The Spanish star said he had not considered withdrawing from the ATP Finals due to the hamstring issue.

“Obviously, it is true that the tests came at a time when I was already qualified. That helped me,” Alcaraz said. “The tests came back fine, which meant we could compete.

“Withdrawing or not being on the table was something that had not been considered, but we really didn’t know how we would cope and how the days would go after the test, after the last group match, after the semi-finals.

“The body can react in any way and we had to be ready for everything. That kind of decision, that kind of thought, that uncertainty is what made this week a little more difficult than it should have been.”

The former world No 1 also hailed the importance of his team.

“I had a big part of my team here, a big part of my family, who calmed me down, who gave me the desire, who gave me peace of mind, and that has been a fundamental part of me being here today with the trophy,” he added.

Spain will face Austria in the Davis Cup quarter-finals on Thursday.

title: WTA Singles World Rankings - complete list: Elena Rybakina reigns as queen of the court to end 2026 season
Alcaraz gains ground on Sinner following Turin title, Mover of Week
article_text:
World No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz finished the 2026 ATP Tour season on a 14-match winning streak, claiming consecutive titles in Vienna, Paris and at the coveted Nitto ATP Finals, where he sealed his first triumph at the year-end event.

The Spaniard’s late-season surge has helped him close the gap on World No. 2 and rival Jannik Sinner.

For the final time this year, ATPTour.com looks at the movers of the week in the PIF ATP Rankings, as of Monday 23 November.

Alcaraz completed a perfect campaign in Turin on Sunday, finishing 5-0 for the week and defeating World No. 1 Alexander Zverev in the championship match.

Having begun the Nitto ATP Finals trailing World No. 2 Sinner by 1,850 PIF ATP Ranking points, Alcaraz is now only 350 points behind the Italian. The 30-time tour-level titlist Alcaraz holds 7,600 PIF ATP Rankings points.

Zverev claimed ATP Year-End No. 1 presented by PIF honours, receiving that trophy in Turin. After a runner-up finish at the Nitto ATP Finals, the German holds 10,350 PIF ATP Ranking points. He is 2,400 points ahead of World No. 2 Sinner.

Having reached the last four in Turin, Shelton consolidated his position at World No. 4. Competing at the Nitto ATP Finals for the second consecutive year, Shelton improved upon last year's 0-3 showing with a semi-final run. Shelton's only losses in Turin this year were to Zverev and Alcaraz. The US Open finalist earned 400 points last week.

Fils, 22, made his Nitto ATP Finals debut and became the first Frenchman to earn a match win at the event since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011. Fils moved up one place in the PIF ATP Rankings and is now at a career-high No. 6.

Following his 10th career ATP Challenger title, Seyboth Wild is back inside the Top 100. The 26-year-old Brazilian was crowned champion at the Montevideo Challenger on Sunday. He was one of seven Challenger champions last week, alongside Toby Samuel, Francesco Passaro, Yosuke Watanuki, Dylan Dietrich, Sebastian Gorzny and Oliver Tarvet.

title: India at 2026 BWF World Tour with Nine Titles as Lakshya Sen, Sindhu Lead Resurgence
article_text:
India has secured nine BWF World Tour titles across Super 750, Super 500 and Super 300 tournaments in 2026, placing 11th in the global standings.

Lakshya Sen, PV Sindhu and the doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty have led India's campaign, which reflects a significant improvement in the country's international badminton performances.

India's badminton campaign in 2026 has witnessed a notable resurgence, with players across singles and men's doubles contributing to a nine-title haul on the BWF World Tour. While the country currently occupies 11th position in the overall national standings, its performances at the Super 750 and Super 500 levels underline the growing competitiveness of Indian badminton.

According to the latest title standings through November 22, India has won three Super 750, three Super 500 and three Super 300 titles. However, the absence of a Super 1000 championship and titles at the Super 100 level has prevented India from making a stronger impact on the overall rankings.

China leads the standings with 57 titles, followed by South Korea with 17 and Chinese Taipei with 13. India's nine-title tally places it behind France, which has eight titles but a superior distribution of victories at the higher tournament levels.

Two of India's biggest singles stars, Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu, have played central roles in the country's 2026 campaign. Sen has won two Super 500 titles, capturing the Hylo Open and Japan Masters during November. His consecutive victories towards the end of the season have been particularly important, helping him secure qualification for the prestigious BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, scheduled from December 9 to 13.

The Indian also came close to a major Super 1000 breakthrough at the All England Open, reaching the men's singles final before losing to Chinese Taipei's Lin Chun-yi 15-21, 20-22.

That defeat highlighted the narrow margins separating Sen from the biggest titles on the international circuit. Nevertheless, his November performances have demonstrated his ability to compete consistently against the world's leading shuttlers. Sindhu has also enjoyed an encouraging season, winning the Japan Open (Super 750) and Hylo Open (Super 500). Her return to the winner's podium at two different tournament levels has been an important development for Indian women's badminton.

Together, Sen and Sindhu have contributed four of India's nine titles, demonstrating the importance of experienced international campaigners in the country's overall performance.

India's men's doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty has delivered two Super 750 titles in 2026. The pair won the Singapore Open and China Masters, reinforcing their position among the world's leading men's doubles combinations.

Their victories have been particularly valuable because India has struggled to produce comparable results in other doubles disciplines this season. Despite the success of Satwik and Chirag, India has not secured a single World Tour title in women's doubles or mixed doubles across the completed tournaments.

This remains an important area for improvement, especially considering the strength of countries such as China, South Korea, Malaysia and Indonesia in the doubles categories.

India's nine championships have been distributed across three tournament levels and three playing categories.

One of the encouraging aspects of India's campaign has been the emergence of younger women's singles players.

Devika Sihag won the Thailand Masters, and Tanvi Sharma captured the Taipei Open, while Ashmita Chaliha claimed the Korea Masters title. These victories demonstrate that India's women's singles depth extends beyond established names such as Sindhu. The emergence of younger champions is particularly important as the country builds towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic cycle.

The national standings use a tier-based ranking methodology rather than simply ordering countries by their total number of trophies. Super 1000 titles carry the highest priority, followed by Super 750, Super 500, Super 300 and Super 100 championships.

This explains why Canada occupies ninth position with just two titles, ahead of France and India, despite both countries having higher overall trophy counts. France is ranked 10th with eight titles, including four Super 750 championships. India follows in 11th position with nine titles but only three Super 750 victories.

China's dominance is driven by its extraordinary depth, particularly in women's doubles and mixed doubles. South Korea, meanwhile, has relied heavily on An Se-young and its successful men's doubles combinations.

For India, the absence of a Super 1000 title remains the biggest gap. Sen's All England final appearance and Satwik-Chirag's Super 750 success show that the country is capable of challenging at the highest level, but converting those performances into the biggest titles remains the next objective.

India still has opportunities to improve its overall title tally before the 2026 season concludes. The Syed Modi International, scheduled in Lucknow from November 24 to 29, will be followed by the Guwahati Masters from December 1 to 6 and the Odisha Masters from December 8 to 13.

These tournaments provide opportunities for Indian players to add to their championship count, particularly in the Super 300 and Super 100 categories. However, under the existing tier-based ranking methodology, additional Super 300 and Super 100 victories cannot bridge India's deficit to France, which has four Super 750 titles compared to India's three.

The BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou will therefore be particularly significant for the final standings, with Lakshya Sen representing India's challenge. India's nine-title campaign is already a considerable improvement on its position entering the closing stages of the previous season. With five of its nine victories coming in women's singles and two each in men's singles and men's doubles, the results also reveal the areas where the country has developed the most.

title: Badminton: Rexy wants Pearly-Thinaah to carry mental growth into World Tour Finals
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: Skill wins you points, but keeping your emotions in check wins you titles.

And that is the positive change that national doubles coaching director Rexy Mainaky saw in national women’s doubles aces Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah as they reclaimed the Hong Kong Open crown on Sunday (Nov 22).

"They have learnt to focus on how to handled thing when they were not going well on court," said Rexy.

"They have learnt to stay motivated and help each other through those difficult moments."

The world No. 4 pair had to hold their nerve in the final at the Kai Tak Arena, saving a game point in the opener before beating Japan’s Sumire Nakade-Miyu Takahashi in straight games.

It was the closest they came to dropping a game all week as they reclaimed the crown they first won in 2024.

Pearly-Thinaah have had their share of setbacks and comebacks over the years.

They won the 2022 French Open less than two months after Pearly injured her hamstring.

A back injury sidelined Pearly again in April this year, but the pair have since won the Denmark and Hong Kong Opens.

These victories took their tally to three titles this year, following their Indonesia Masters win in January.

And Rexy hoped they would continue to show improvement when they get ready for the season-ending World Tour Finals in Hangzhou from Dec 9-13.

Pearly-Thinaah will aim to better last year’s run to the semi-finals, their best showing at the tournament.

"They have plenty of experience in these situations," said Rexy.

"My advice is to stay focused and learn from the way they played to win the Denmark and Hong Kong Opens," said Rexy.

Pearly acknowledged that they have learnt to stay composed when things went against them during a heart-to-heart after their first round exit at the Japan Masters.

Staying calm also helped Pearly vary her attack in Hong Kong, bringing out the trick shots she learnt as a junior from her father and first coach, Tan Seng Hoe.

"My father taught me those skills when I was young," said Pearly.

"I can use them effectively when I remain calm, but sometimes, when I become too eager to win, I tend to forget about them."

title: Anders Antonsen claims Hong Kong Open title without playing final
article_text:
Denmark's Anders Antonsen secured his third BWF World Tour title of 2026 on Sunday, but not quite in the way he had hoped. The Dane was crowned Hong Kong Open champion after his final opponent, Kunlavut Vitidsarn, was forced to withdraw due to injury.

The highly anticipated men's singles final between Antonsen and Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn never took place, as the Thai star withdrew with a back injury before the scheduled match.

It was an unusual ending to an otherwise impressive week for Antonsen, who had battled his way through several challenging matches to reach the final.

Speaking to Danish broadcaster TV 2 Sport, Antonsen expressed his disappointment at missing out on the opportunity to face Vitidsarn.

"It's frustrating. It's very anticlimactic. I had been looking forward to today's match so much. I was really excited and thought it would be a great experience, and, as so many times before, a thrilling match against Kunlavut Vitidsarn. This wasn't the way I had hoped to win," Antonsen told TV 2 Sport.

The Dane survived a thrilling quarterfinal against China's Zhu Xuan Chen, winning 21-18, 14-21, 24-22, before delivering a convincing 21-13, 21-13 victory over India's Lakshya Sen in the semifinals.

Although the title came without a final being played, the result adds another trophy to Antonsen's collection ahead of the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals in December, where he will be joint by follow europeans Christo Popov and world champion Alex Lanier.

While the men's singles final was never played, the remaining four finals produced their champions on Sunday.

In women's singles, China's Wang Zhi Yi successfully defended her title, defeating Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong 21-16, 21-11.

Malaysia celebrated two titles, with Man Wei Chong/Tee Kai Wun winning the men's doubles against Indonesia's Leo Rolly Carnando/Daniel Marthin 21-19, 21-18.

Their compatriots Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan also claimed the women's doubles title, defeating Japan's Sumire Nakade/Miyu Takahashi 22-20, 21-16.

Finally, China's Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping secured the mixed doubles title after a three-game victory over compatriots Jiang Zhen Bang/Wei Ya Xin, winning 17-21, 21-9, 21-15.

title: ATP Rankings: Alexander Zverev misses opportunity, Carlos Alcaraz closes gap to Jannik Sinner
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has finished the 2026 season on a high by winning the final trophy on offer, the ATP Finals, and with it he finds himself right on the heels of Jannik Sinner in the rankings.

The seven-time Grand Slam winner defeated world No 1 Alexander Zverev in the final to win the season-ending event for the first time in his career and with it came a handy 1,500 ranking points as he won the tournament undefeated.

As a result, Alcaraz is now just 350 points behind second-placed Sinner – who missed the tournament due to injury – while Zverev has a comfortable 2,400-point advantage over the Italian.

The Spaniard finished the year with three consecutive titles as he also won the Vienna Open and Paris Masters and, when asked if he feels like the No 1, he replied: “Well, no, not at all.

“What I’m going to say is I think everybody feels he’s the No 1. Me, Sascha, Jannik,[Ben] Shelton, I think everybody thinks they are the No 1 in the world.

“And I think that confidence, it’s really important. Having that confidence in yourself, it’s really important. When you hit the practice court, when you hit the match, it’s really important to have that confidence yourself.

“You know, the No 1 is Sascha. He really deserves it. Nobody’s going to take that position and the No 1 away from him. We have to think about it. We have to say that. Right now, the ranking says it’s Sascha, and we have to give credit to him.”

Despite his emphatic title run in Turin, Alcaraz won’t be able to return to No 1 after next year’s Australian Open – even if he successfully defends his trophy – as he has 2,000 points to defend while Zverev will drop only 800 points.

Zverev would have secured the post-Australian Open No 1 spot had he won the ATP Finals.

However, the German is all but assured of remaining top as Sinner would need to enter and win an ATP 500 event before the season-opening Grand Slam and then go on to win the Melbourne Park tournament.

At this stage, it is not even a given that the Italian will play at the Australian Open due to his knee injury.

Outside of the top three, Shelton is a comfortable fourth as he has a 1,350-point lead over Daniil Medvedev while Arthur Fils finishes at a career-high No 6 as he moved up one spot with his one win at the ATP Finals.

Flavio Cobolli, Frances Tiafoe, Taylor Fritz and Rafael Jodar complete the top 10.

Tennis great Novak Djokovic ends the season at a disappointing 12th – his lowest year-end finish since 2006 – with the China Open his only trophy while he finished runner-up to Alcaraz at the Australian Open.

title: Lakshya Sen On Podium For Third Time With Hong Kong Open 2026 Bronze
article_text:
Lakshya Sen won bronze at the Hong Kong Open 2026 after losing the semifinal to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen, who became men’s singles champion.

Indian ace Lakshya Sen finished on the podium for the third time in the last month. Lakshya ended his Hong Kong Open 2026 campaign with a bronze medal in the men’s singles. Sen’s third-place finish came after losing to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen in the Super 500 semifinals. Anders went on to win the Hong Kong championship after Thailand’s second seed, Kunlavut Vitidsarn, withdrew due to injury concerns. Lakshya, ranked World No. 11 in the latest BWF World Rankings, has already secured his place at the BWF World Tour Finals before the semifinals. The Finals will be held in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December.

The World No.3 Danish player has also qualified for the World Tour Finals. He is ranked 4th for the Hangzhou Finals. He defeated Sen with 21-13 and 21-13 in both sets, winning the men’s singles semifinals. Sen’s campaign ended with a bronze medal in the Hong Kong Open. The final did not happen at the Super 500 as Kunlavut pulled out due to injury, and Antonsen was declared the winner.

Sen moved to sixth place in the Race to Finals standings after winning back-to-back BWF titles. The 25-year-old won the Hylo Open 2026 men’s singles title in Germany, and two weeks later he won the Kumamoto Masters 2026 in Japan.

In the women’s singles, two-time Asian Champion, China’s Wang Zhiyi defended her title and defeated Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong. Chochuwong beat India’s Rakshitha Ramraj in the quarterfinals. The 19-year-old won against World No.4 in her previous match, making it a memorable outing for her.

Indian shuttlers now turn to the Syed Modi India International in Lucknow from 24 to 29 November.

title: Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu Qualify for BWF World Tour Finals 2026, India Set for Two-Pronged Challenge in Hangzhou
article_text:
India will have two representatives at the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals, with Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu securing qualification for the prestigious season-ending tournament scheduled to take place in Hangzhou, China, from December 9 to 13.

Sen will compete in men’s singles, while Sindhu has booked her place in women’s singles. Their qualification marks an important moment for Indian badminton, with both players returning to the year-end championship for the first time since 2021.

The two berths also reflect contrasting but equally encouraging stories. Sen secured his place through a strong finish to the season, winning consecutive Super 500 titles in Germany and Japan. Sindhu, meanwhile, has rebuilt her form following an injury-disrupted period, returning to the world’s top six and producing some of her most consistent badminton in recent seasons.

With eight players competing in each singles discipline, the World Tour Finals bring together the season’s most successful performers for one final test.

For Lakshya Sen, qualification represents a significant turnaround after an inconsistent middle phase of the season.

The Indian began 2026 with an impressive run at the All England Open, reaching the final after defeating established opponents, including Shi Yuqi and Victor Lai. He eventually finished runner-up to Taiwan’s Lin Chun-yi.

However, a series of early exits at major tournaments and a shoulder injury disrupted his campaign. His withdrawal from the French Open in October further complicated his qualification prospects.

Sen responded with an outstanding finish, winning the Hylo Open in Germany before claiming the Kumamoto Masters Japan title. At the Hylo Open, he defeated Indonesia’s Jonatan Christie 21–17, 21–10 in the final, becoming the first Indian to win the tournament twice. In Japan, he continued his momentum by defeating Koki Watanabe in the title match.

The back-to-back titles transformed his position in the HSBC Race to Finals standings.

Sen entered the Hong Kong Open as the sixth-ranked player in the Race to Finals, holding 74,180 points. His qualification was subsequently confirmed after compatriot Kidambi Srikanth defeated Japan’s Koki Watanabe, one of the players challenging for the final qualification positions.

Sen continued his Hong Kong campaign, reaching the semifinals before losing to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen.

The 25-year-old will now return to the World Tour Finals after making his debut in 2021, when he reached the semifinals. His recent performances suggest that he will arrive in Hangzhou with considerable confidence.

The men's singles field is particularly competitive, featuring defending champion Christo Popov, Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan, Canada’s Victor Lai, Antonsen, Chou Tien-chen and Thailand’s Kunlavut Vitidsarn. Reigning World Champion Alex Lanier also qualifies through the automatic exemption.

Sindhu’s qualification is another major positive for Indian badminton.

The two-time Olympic medallist has worked her way back into the elite group after an injury-affected period that interrupted her progress. Her 2026 season has been built around consistency, with 10 quarterfinal appearances, two titles and a return to World No. 6.

Her most significant victories came at the Japan Open Super 750 and Hylo Open Super 500. At the Japan Open, Sindhu defeated Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–17 in the final to claim an important title.

She also demonstrated her ability to challenge the very best by taking world No. 1 An Se-young to three games in the French Open final, eventually losing 21–16, 11–21, 12–21.

Sindhu’s return to the World Tour Finals carries additional significance. She remains the only Indian player to have won the women’s singles title, having lifted the trophy in 2018 in Guangzhou.

Ranked fifth in the Race to Finals, she will enter the Hangzhou competition with the experience of having competed against the world's leading players for more than a decade.

The women's singles field will be led by South Korea’s An Se-young, who has enjoyed a remarkable 2026 season. The defending champion and reigning World Champion has dominated the circuit, making her the leading contender for another title.

China’s Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei, Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi and Tomoka Miyazaki, and Thailand’s Ratchanok Intanon and Pornpawee Chochuwong will add further depth to the competition.

While India’s singles representation is encouraging, the country will have no entries in the three doubles disciplines.

The biggest disappointment is the absence of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. The former world No. 1 pair won two Super 750 titles during 2026, at the Singapore Open and China Masters, but finished outside the qualification positions after competing in a reduced tournament schedule.

Their workload management and commitments to national team events affected their Race to Finals ranking.

India’s women’s doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, despite winning a bronze medal at the 2026 World Championships, also missed qualification.

The 2026 World Tour Finals will feature eight qualifiers in each discipline, divided into two groups of four. The group stage will be followed by semifinals and finals, with the championship concluding on December 13.

The tournament carries total prize money of USD 3.5 million, underlining its status as one of the most prestigious events on the badminton calendar.

For India, the challenge will rest on Sen’s late-season momentum and Sindhu’s experience at the highest level. Both have already demonstrated that they can compete with the world’s best.

The next step is to convert that form into a strong finish in Hangzhou. With two singles players back among the season’s elite, Indian badminton will have another opportunity to end 2026 on a high.

title: Gauff, Townsend Clinch USA BJK Cup Victory over Hungary
article_text:
Coco Gauff created a happy homecoming weekend in Delray Beach.

Delray Beach native Coco Gauff and Taylor Townsend clinched Billie Jean King Cup Qualifying victory for the U.S. on Sunday, defeating Hungarian doubles pair Anna Bondar and Dalma Galfi 6-4, 6-3 at the Delray Beach Tennis Center.

Ashlyn Krueger, ranked No. 41 in the world, capped the tie with a 6-2, 6-1, dead singles win over Adrienn Nagy, giving captain Lindsay Davenport a clean sweep in the tie.

“I think there was always this scenario that we would probably be up 2-0. Once that was the scenario, I was, like, of course, I’m going to play and try to just finish it 3-0,” Gauff said. “Yeah, I think we were both prepared to play with each other. We didn’t know what the end of Day 1 results would

have looked like. Maybe if it was 1-All, maybe I would have not played, because I would have had to play singles

30 minutes later. But, you know, it’s always that risk.

“I feel like Taylor and Lindsay were confident in my ability to play in doubles and potentially have to play singles after, but I’m really happy that they trusted me to step in and make the change. But, yeah, I’m really happy that I got to play with Taylor today.”

The U.S. joins seven nations advancing out of the Playoffs to the 2027 Qualifiers. The Qualifiers will be played in April, with the specific dates and ties to be announced.

title: Badminton: Pearly-Thinaah savour booster ahead of tough test at World Tour Finals
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: National women’s doubles aces Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah could not have picked a better time to rediscover their form and rhythm.

The world No. 4 pair reclaimed the Hong Kong Open crown yesterday, defeating Japan’s Sumire Nakade-Miyu Takahashi 22-20, 21-16 in 40 minutes at the Kai Tak Arena.

Winning the crown without dropping a game puts them in good stead ahead of next month’s season-ending World Tour Finals.

“It’s definitely a confidence boost for the World Tour Finals,” said Thinaah.

It was sweet revenge for the 2024 champions, who lost to the Japanese pair in the Taipei Open final in August.

The victory brought them their third title of the year and second in five weeks, following triumphs at the Indonesia Masters in January and Denmark Open last month.

Their unbeaten run in Hong Kong marked a welcome turnaround after a disappointing first-round exit at last week’s Japan Masters.

“This week, we really wanted to put last week behind us, come in fresh and be more focused.”

A heart-to-heart talk helped them regroup, with Pearly taking satisfaction in how they handled difficult situations and managed their emotions throughout the week.

That composure showed in the final when they saved a game point at 19-20 despite Pearly breaking her racquet.

They then pulled away from 14-14 in the second game to seal the title.

“There were still ups and downs in the first few matches, but the way we managed them was really positive,” said Thinaah.

“There was also a lot of communication between us, which really helped throughout the week.”

A sterner examination awaits at the Finals in Hangzhou from Dec 9-13, with China’s Liu Shengshu-Tan Ning, world champions Baek Ha-na-Lee So-hee of South Korea and Japan’s Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto among the qualified contenders.

Fukushima-Matsumoto ended the Malaysians’ breakthrough semi-final run last year.

Pearly-Thinaah had previously exited at the group stage in 2021, 2022 and 2024, while missing qualification in 2023.

“We want to go back and focus on the next two weeks. There are still many things we need to work on.”

“These will be two crucial weeks for both of us – learning, supporting each other and handling our emotions. We’re really excited for the World Tour Finals,” added Thinaah.

title: Brooks Koepka swipes Bryson DeChambeau over match fail: 'Didn't hole a putt the entire time'
article_text:
Before the rise of LIV Golf, Brooks Koepka and Bryson DeChambeau had one of the best (and most contentious) rivalries in pro golf.

The clashes between the major champions were not restricted to the golf course.

After Koepka followed DeChambeau to LIV, though, the former rivals seemed to transform into partners, at least publicly.

Now that LIV Golf is no more, however, the feud between the two stars is ratcheting up again.

Last month, Koepka zinged DeChambeau during a podcast appearance, saying Bryson “lives in his own world.”

On Tuesday, Koepka was at it again, taking another swipe at the two-time U.S. Open winner during a press conference for the upcoming Skins Game.

Koepka is prepping to take part in the second edition of the reborn Skins Game (known as the Farmers Insurance Skins Game) the day after Thanksgiving.

But in a press conference previewing the Black Friday match, Koepka got to talking about another pro-golf exhibition from the recent past: the 2024 Crypto.com Showdown at Shadow Creek. That event pitted Koepka and DeChambeau, who were LIV Golf pros at the time, against PGA Tour stars Rory McIlroy and Scottie Scheffler.

McIlroy and Scheffler handily beat Koepka and DeChambeau, earning about $5 million each in crypto tokens. Brooks and Bryson walked away with nothing.

During his press conference ahead of this week’s Skins Game, Koepka was asked about his experience at the Showdown. In his response, he blamed the loss on Bryson’s poor putting.

“Since I did not win, my teammate didn’t hole a putt the entire time, so I did not receive any of that,” Koepka said, taking a jab at DeChambeau.

He then said that it’s “great” that the Skins Game is “individual” instead of a team event like the Showdown, where he “didn’t get to choose” his teammate.

“Which is great because it’s an individual thing this time. So I’m more excited about that, but it’ll be fun,” Koepka said.

The comments come just weeks after Koepka joined the “Dan on Golf” podcast and threw more shade DeChambeau’s way.

DeChambeau famously complained that Rory McIlroy did not speak with him when they were paired together during the final round of the 2025 Masters.

Koepka had a unique explanation for McIlroy’s silent treatment, blaming it on DeChambeau.

“Well, I mean, [DeChambeau] lives in his own world. I mean, I don’t think many people want to talk to him regardless,” Koepka said.

So when will we next get to see Koepka and DeChambeau tee it up against each other? It might be a while. Koepka will be playing the PGA Tour next year, after rejoining ahead the 2026 season. DeChambeau, on the other hand, will play the DP World Tour for most of 2027. So, unless DeChambeau gets offered an accelerated path back to the PGA Tour, we won’t seem them in the same field until the 2027 Masters.

Koepka will face off against Justin Thomas, Wyndham Clark and Jackson Koivun in the Farmers Insurance Skins Game on Friday, Nov. 27.

title: Brooks Koepka rule improves pro's PGA Tour status for 2027
article_text:
Max McGreevy had just emptied the tank on the final day of the PGA Tour season. After a year in which he made 19 of 31 cuts but failed to produce any stellar results, the 31-year-old had needed to put together a good final round at the RSM Classic to give himself a chance at retaining some semblance of PGA Tour status.

But an even-par 70 at Sea Island left McGreevy tied for 10th. It was his best finish of the season but one that didn’t seem like it was going to be good enough to nudge him inside the top 125 to keep conditional status on the PGA Tour. When McGreevy walked off the course, he was bouncing between No. 126 and 127 in the FedEx Cup Fall standings. Those few spots are a huge difference — between getting 15-20 PGA Tour starts, as Lanto Griffin did in 2026 (17 starts) after finishing 125th last year, or largely plying your trade on the Korn Ferry Tour, as Frankie Capan III (only six PGA Tour starts), who finished 127th in 2025, did this year.

After the final round of his season, McGreevy spoke with the press about life on the bubble and how, after a subpar season, he was willing to face the repercussions for his below-average play.

“Just think your life can kind of change any week that you get out here, so as well as you can play and get every opportunity that you can get next year,” McGreevy said. “Unfortunately, I’m not going to finish where I wanted to at the end of the year, but hopefully get a couple starts, and if that’s the case, then hopefully I can take advantage when that happens. If I’ve got to go play more on the Korn Ferry Tour, golf is golf, life is life. We’ll go forward from here and yeah, try to keep moving up.”

An hour or so later, Marco Penge won a four-way playoff to end the season and finalize the rankings. There sat McGreevy at 126, seemingly one spot off the mark. In the end, though, he landed precisely where he needed. A one-year wrinkle due to the return of Brooks Koepka meant that McGreevy’s T10 finish at the RSM and No. 126 place in the FedEx Fall rankings was good enough to sneak into the conditional 111-125 category.

When Koepka returned from LIV Golf in January via the “Returning Members Program,” the PGA Tour wanted to make sure that his reintegration did not hurt its current members. As part of the return agreement, the Tour added two players to the field each time Koepka teed it up. The Tour also did not want Koepka’s return to affect another player’s ranking or eligibility in 2027, so they added a stipulation that any player who finished behind Koepka in the final rankings would move up one spot in the standings. The five-time major champion finished the year at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup Fall. That meant that Jason Day, who battled an injury in 2026, moved up from 111 to 110, which will give him conditional status in a category that doesn’t reshuffle; Day could also use a career money exemption in 2027.

Koepka’s return also meant that McGreevy, who finished 126th, will move up to 125th and, in 2027, be able to play out of that conditional category, which is subject to reshuffle.

That one spot can be the difference between a season grinding on the KFT vs. getting a decent chunk of starts on the PGA Tour. McGreevy’s T10 finish at the RSM put him two points ahead of Joel Dahmen for the final spot in the 111-125 category. That’s a one-shot difference between dropping back down and facing an uphill climb or holding on. McGreevy’s 70 on a windy Monday at Sea Island was good enough for him to finish three strokes better than Dahmen and one spot ahead in the final FedEx Cup rankings. With Koepka’s help, McGreevy barely held on instead of having to deal with a harsh reality of pro golf.

“If anything, as I’ve gotten older, I’m playing older, which I don’t necessarily think is a great suit for me,” McGreevy said of what he learned from a down 2026. “Ten years playing now, I think I have enough scar tissue to know when to take advantage and when to not. I’ve watched the young kids out here, and they’re just, they go 24/7 type of thing. I think I played a little bit more reserved than I probably should have all year. I made a lot of cuts, which is good for me; I’m usually pretty streaky. I just think I took my foot off the gas pedal a little too much this year and hopefully we can learn from that and just kind of move forward with it.”

Koepka’s return and two-point advantage over Dahmen gave McGreevy a professional lifeline in 2027. It’s up to him to make the most of it.
